## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file

Yes — both, for both Zimmermann repos. Two separate access routes, and it's worth knowing the difference:

**1. The app's session index** (MCP session tools)
`list_sessions` / `search_session_transcripts` / `list_events` — full-text search across transcripts and read any one of them. Returns **53 named sessions**, ~46 of them Zimmermann (`ZIMM - PR #70`, `ZIMM - Contentful Setup`, `ZIMM - Guardrails`, etc., back to `ZIMM - Dev Onboard Checklist` on 2026-07-15). **This index does not include agent sessions.**

**2. Raw transcripts on disk** (`~/.claude/projects/`) — this is the exhaustive one

| | zimmermann-pwa | Zimmermann-Handover |
|---|---|---|
| Top-level sessions | **399** (987 MB) | **119** (379 MB) |
| Sessions that spawned agents | 46 | 15 |
| Agent transcripts | **268** | **41** |
| Range | 2026-07-09 → today | 2026-07-13 → today |

Agent sessions live at `<session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` with a `.meta.json` sidecar carrying `agentType`, `description`, and `spawnDepth` — so I can tell *what each agent was asked to do* without reading its whole transcript. Breakdown for pwa: 199 `general-purpose`, 65 `Explore`, 2 `Plan`, 2 `fork`.

**Two caveats worth flagging:**

- **53 vs 399.** The sidebar index only tracks named sessions; forks, resumes, and short/untitled ones exist only as files. If you mean *all* sessions, I have to work from disk, not the session tools.
- **1.4 GB total.** Far beyond what I can load. So it's search-and-excerpt, not read-everything — I grep for what you're after and pull the relevant spans. Works well; just means I need a reasonably specific target.

What are you trying to pull out of them?

content.text:
Scanned all 399 pwa-kit sessions plus the 268 agent transcripts. Your read on the pattern is correct — but the data says something you may not expect, so let me lead with that.

## You already built this plan. Six weeks ago.

`zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/` has **14 skills** in it, dated Jul 15 – Aug 19. Well-written ones, with real descriptions.

Across 399 sessions there were **85 Skill invocations total** — about 0.2 per session. And:

| Skill | Invocations |
|---|---|
| `code-review` | 28 |
| `session-start` | 22 |
| `code-quality` | 12 |
| `pr-checklist` | 11 |
| `generate-changelog` | 3 |
| **`audit-tier`, `scope-check`, `new-component`, `feature-spec`, `qa-generate`, `onboarding`, `project-init`, `contentful-register-component`, `upstream-sync-review`** | **0** |

Nine of fourteen have never fired once. `session-start` — whose own description says *"use at the start of every coding session"* — fired in 22 of 399 sessions. About 5%.

So "build a set of skills I reach for" is not an untested idea. It's a tested one, and the reaching-for is where it broke. Building fourteen more gets you twenty-eight skills and eighty-five invocations.

## Why the five survivors survived

The ones that stuck all share a shape: **a named deliverable at an unmistakable moment.** "Review this PR." "Write the PR description." You *know* you're at that moment, so you reach.

The nine that died split into rituals (`session-start`, `project-init`, `onboarding`) and scaffolds (`new-component`, `audit-tier`, `scope-check`). A ritual you have to *remember to invoke* isn't a ritual — it's another thing to remember, which is the exact fatigue you're trying to remove.

## The bigger gap: your #1 workload has no skill at all

Clustering how your sessions open:

| Workload | Sessions |
|---|---|
| **Research → verify → report** (codebase + Confluence + Jira) | **116** |
| Branch / repo hygiene | 95 |
| Jira ticket / user story work | 82 |
| PR / code review | 30 |
| Meeting prep & in-meeting capture | 28 |

That top row is your job, and you've hand-typed its incantation ~99 times. Verbatim samples:

- `execute an in-depth analysis across the codebase, confluence, and JIRA…`
- `execute an in-depth check of the codebase + confluence + and jira…`
- `execute an in-depth full-on exhaustive check…`
- `execute an in-depth, verbose, and authoritative scan…`
- `execute an in-depth v&v/check/audit into the codebase, codebase docs, codebase config, confluence, and JIRA…`

**That drift is the inconsistency risk you sensed.** Not a missed step — a moving depth setting. "In-depth" and "in-depth full-on exhaustive" are different instructions, so the same question asked twice gets researched to two different standards. Tool counts confirm this is the real workload: ~3,500 Atlassian calls against 26,117 Bash calls. None of your 14 skills touches it.

## The asset you're undervaluing

502 Agent invocations, and their descriptions are remarkable: `Verify guardrail claims to file:line locations`, `V&V doc vs codebase/configs`, `Stage1 validate → Stage2 implement → Stage3 regression verification`, `Wave1 scope ledger` → `Wave2 adversarial reconciliation`, `Agent A/B/C/D` split audits.

You have a genuine claims-must-be-verified-to-file:line discipline, and you're already running staged multi-agent loops by hand. **You don't need to import loop engineering — you're doing it.** What you need is to stop rebuilding the harness from scratch each time.

## What I'd actually do

1. **Fix invocation before authoring.** Anything whose description says "every time" should be a `SessionStart` hook, not a skill — the harness runs it, you don't remember it. That alone converts `session-start` from 5% to 100%.
2. **Write one skill: the research-verify-report loop.** Highest-value single artifact you can produce — 116 sessions of retyping, and it's where the depth drift lives. Bake the depth tiers in (quick / standard / exhaustive) so "how hard should I look" becomes a parameter instead of an adverb.
3. **Then triage the nine dead ones** — some belong as `.claude/rules` (`audit-tier`, `scope-check` are really guardrails), and some may just be genuinely rare and worth deleting.

One caution on loops: they pay off where a **cheap, honest verifier** exists — tests, tsc, lint, CI. Your PR-review and story-shaping work has no such verifier; the verifier is you. Wrapping those in an automated loop mostly buys you confident-sounding iteration. Keep those human-in-the-lead, the way `qa-generate` already says.

Want me to start with the hook conversion and the research-verify-report skill? Or would you rather I first dig into *why* specific dead skills didn't fire — I can pull the sessions where you did that work by hand and see what you typed instead.

content.text:
Makes sense — and it corrects something in my last message that matters.

**Those skills aren't yours.** `git log` on `.claude/skills/` shows TimLavelle (14 commits), Hardi (13), TimLavelleACC (5). Zero from you. So "you already built this plan" was wrong — they're a team artifact, committed to the repo, encoding Tim's and Hardi's model of the codebase. You not reaching for them isn't a discipline lapse; they were never built around your process.

Which makes the invocation data read differently, and better for your case: the five that fired (`code-review`, `session-start`, `code-quality`, `pr-checklist`, `generate-changelog`) are exactly the ones that happen to overlap with lead duties. The nine that never fired are IC and setup work — `new-component`, `contentful-register-component`, `qa-generate`, `onboarding`, `project-init`. You didn't skip them; they're not your job. That's a role mismatch, not a fatigue problem, and a personal layer is the correct fix for it.

## The two layers

| | Team layer | Personal layer |
|---|---|---|
| Where | `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/` (committed) | `~/.claude/skills/` (yours, portable) |
| Answers | "How does *this codebase* do X" | "How does *Marcel* work" |
| Owner | Tim, Hardi | You |
| Scope | Dies with the project | Follows you to Handover, and the next client |

Your personal layer is effectively greenfield right now — `~/.claude/skills/` contains only `playwright-skill`.

**One design rule I'd hold to:** personal skills *orchestrate*, team skills and rules *execute*. Your skill should **cite** `.claude/rules/typescript.md` and `.claude/registry/components.md`, never copy their contents. The moment you paste Tim's conventions into your personal skill, you've forked the team's standards into a private copy that silently rots the next time he edits the original — and you'd be reviewing PRs against a stale bar without knowing it. Reference, don't duplicate. That also keeps your skills portable: on the next project they bind to whatever rules exist there.

## Sources, ranked

1. **Your 399 sessions** — the strongest source by far, and the only one that records what you *actually* do rather than what you'd say you do. The ~99 hand-typed research incantations are literally the spec for your flagship skill, drift and all.
2. **`.docs/prompts/`** — worth a look; that may already be you saving your own prompts.
3. **`.claude/rules/` (11 files) + `.claude/registry/` (5)** — not content to absorb, but the things your skills should point at. Note `squadA.md` / `squadB.md` — squad ownership is lead-relevant.
4. **The 14 team skills** — read for mechanics and for the quality bar you're reviewing against.

## What I'd expect the personal set to be

From your own workload distribution, these are all role-shaped rather than codebase-shaped — none of them belong in the team repo:

- **research-verify-report** (116 sessions) — the flagship, with depth as a parameter instead of an adverb
- **pr-review-as-lead** (30) — wraps the team's `code-review`, adds your approval judgment
- **story-shaping / ticket intake** (82)
- **meeting prep & capture** (28)
- **branch & repo hygiene** (95) — possibly just a hook, not a skill

Does that match the set you had in mind, or is your list different? If it's roughly right, I'd start by mining those ~99 research prompts into a single spec — that's the one where the evidence is richest and the repetition cost is highest.

# UI Build — Knowledge & Context

Technical reference only — no roles, no process, no review workflow. Those live in
`fedLead-playbook.md` (the role) and `fedBuild-manual.md` (the procedure).

Every claim here was measured against the installed toolchain, not inherited from an
earlier note. Beliefs that turned out to be wrong are marked **[CORRECTED]** and the
correction is kept visible rather than silently overwritten — a claim that was confidently
wrong once is worth flagging so it isn't re-derived.

     "The lead role: what you say, to whom, and when. Judgement and process, not procedure."),
]

# sibling-file cross-references -> in-document part references.
# NB: zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md is a RETIRED external doc; never rewrite it.
XREF = [
    (re.compile(r'`uiBuild-knowledge\.md`\s*(§\d+)'), r'Part I \1'),
    (re.compile(r'`fedBuild-manual\.md`\s*(§\d+)'),   r'Part II \1'),
    (re.compile(r'`fedLead-playbook\.md`\s*(§\d+)'),  r'Part III \1'),
    (re.compile(r'`uiBuild-knowledge\.md`'),          r'Part I'),
    (re.compile(r'`fedBuild-manual\.md`'),            r'Part II'),
    (re.compile(r'`fedLead-playbook\.md`'),           r'Part III'),
]

def slug(s):
    s = s.strip().lower()
    s = s.replace("&", "").replace("§", "")
    s = re.sub(r"[^\w\s-]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"[\s_]+", "-", s)
    return re.sub(r"-+", "-", s).strip("-")

def process(path, drop_companion_block):
    """Demote headings by one level, drop the H1, rewrite sibling xrefs.
    Fence-aware so '#' comments inside code blocks are never touched."""
    lines = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
    out, toc = [], []
    fence = None
    dropped_h1 = False
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        m = re.match(r'^(\s*)(`{3,}|~{3,})', ln)
        if m:
            tok = m.group(2)[0]
            if fence is None: fence = tok
            elif fence == tok: fence = None
            out.append(ln); i += 1; continue

        if fence is None:
            if not dropped_h1 and re.match(r'^# ', ln):
                dropped_h1 = True; i += 1
                continue
            # drop the now-meaningless "Companions:" pointer block
            if drop_companion_block and ln.startswith("**Companions:**"):
                while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() != "":
                    i += 1
                continue
            h = re.match(r'^(#{2,5}) (.*)$', ln)
            if h:
                lvl, txt = len(h.group(1)), h.group(2)
                if lvl == 2: toc.append(txt)
                ln = "#" * (lvl + 1) + " " + txt
            for pat, rep in XREF:
                ln = pat.sub(rep, ln)
        out.append(ln); i += 1
    return "\n".join(out).strip("\n"), toc

content.text:
I assembled it mechanically rather than retyping, so content loss was structurally impossible, then verified line-by-line: **every substantive line from all three sources is present.** Word count 16,666 → 17,179 (+513, entirely the new preamble and TOC).

**Structure** — one H1, then:

| | Source | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| Part I — UI Build: Knowledge & Context | `uiBuild-knowledge.md` | 77–846 |
| Part II — FED Build Manual | `fedBuild-manual.md` | 847–1657 |
| Part III — FED Lead Playbook | `fedLead-playbook.md` | 1658–2451 |

**What I changed** (only the seams):

- Headings demoted one level — H1 doc → H2 part → H3 section → H4 subsection. Zero level skips. The demotion is fence-aware, so `#` comments inside code blocks were left alone.
- **7 cross-references** rewritten from filenames to part refs: `` `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7 `` → `Part I §7`, and the tier-1 table row → `see Part III`.
- **3 `Companions:` blocks** dropped — they pointed at sibling files that are now sections.
- Added a preamble + linked TOC covering all 45 sections.

**Deliberately preserved:** the two `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` references — that's the *retired* doc, not a sibling, so rewriting them would have been wrong. All `[CORRECTED]` markers and per-document revision footers are intact.

**Three calls I made that you may want different:**

1. **Filename** `fed-handbook.md` — trivial to rename.
2. **Part order** follows the order you listed them (knowledge → procedure → role). That's bottom-up; for reading, role-first is usually better, though for grep-as-a-source it barely matters.
3. **Originals untouched** — all three still sit in `~/Dev`. I didn't delete anything. Worth deciding whether they stay as the editable sources with the handbook regenerated, or whether the handbook becomes canonical and they retire.

The regeneration script is at `scratchpad/merge.py` if you want to re-run it after editing the sources.

One note for what's next: the "Authority on styling" line now appears in the preamble *and* twice inside the parts. I left the in-part copies for fidelity, but when we mine this for skills, that's exactly the sort of thing the skill should point at `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` for rather than restate.

Added 2026-08-29. The SFCC-751 pipeline (PR #61) landed after this manual's 25 Aug baseline, so

#### What actually blocks a merge

`qa.yml` runs five jobs. Only two of them, plus a branch check, are required on `develop`:

| Job (`qa.yml`) | Required? |

Two rules that are easy to get wrong:

1. **The `.feature` comes first and is Lead QA's artifact, not yours.** The `qa-generate` skill
   is explicit that the Gherkin is validated before any Playwright is written. Writing the spec
   first inverts the review and you will be asked to redo it.
2. **Desktop and mobile are separate spec files**, not one file with a viewport loop —
   `SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` under `desktop/` and
   `SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js` under `mobile/`. BrowserStack scopes its matrix to
   real devices, so a viewport loop tests something the matrix doesn't.

`@SFCC-NNN` tag matters beyond CI: an untagged spec reports nothing to Zephyr and the story
looks untested even when it isn't.

going green on a component with no test file is exactly what that looks like.

# `.claude/` asset map — zimmermann-pwa

**Repo root:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`
**Current state:** on branch `develop` @ `269d5d4` (2026-08-29), working tree clean.

Top-level: `skills/` (13 dirs + 1 symlink + README), `rules/` (11 md), `hooks/` (4 sh), `registry/` (5 md + 2 gitignored JSON caches), `settings.json`, `settings.local.json`.

---

## 1. `.claude/skills/` — 14 skills

The 14th is a **symlink**: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/code-review` → `../../.agents/skills/code-review`. It is tracked in git as a symlink and surfaces in the skill list as **`zimmermann-pwa:code-review`** (name-collides with the global `code-review` skill).

### Setup / onboarding

**`session-start`** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/session-start/SKILL.md`
> `description: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.`

- **Does:** 5-step gate — confirm branch (hard stop on `develop`/`main`, line 10), read four `.docs/memory/*` files + `.claude/session-notes.md` in parallel, run health checks, state position in a fixed sentence format, then ask before proceeding. Lines 34–53 also define the **Living Memory write policy**: `.docs/memory/*` is human-owned; `.claude/session-notes.md` is the one file Claude may write directly (gitignored, per-developer).
- **Inputs:** no arguments. Reads `.docs/memory/{projectState,sprintScope,feedback,upstreamBaseline}.md` + `.claude/session-notes.md` (currently absent — expected, skip silently).
- **Outputs:** conversational only. No files.
- **Invokes:** `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` (line 20 — script exists).
- **Callable sub-step:** ✅ **Yes** — the canonical pre-build preamble.

**`onboarding`** — `.claude/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md`
> `description: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.`

- **Does:** 5 phases — role/squad questions, an inline bash environment doctor (lines 34–46: node/npm/claude/coderabbit versions, branch, `.git/hooks` presence, `.env.shared` + six `.env.<tier>` files), then role-branched orientation (Phase 3 dev, Phase 4 QA).
- **Inputs:** no arguments; asks role, squad, new-vs-returning.
- **Outputs:** conversational. Proposes commands, doesn't run the mutating ones.
- **Invokes:** `npm run env -- init`, `npm run env -- dev`, `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, `coderabbit auth login`.
- **Callable sub-step:** ❌ No — but **Phase 2's bash block is worth lifting verbatim** as an environment preflight in your own workflow.

**`project-init`** — `.claude/skills/project-init/SKILL.md`
> `description: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.`

- **Does:** runs the state detector, fixes `[FAIL]`s, then ~9 human questions (Jira prefix, BrowserStack, QA creds, E2E SKUs, Zephyr product, LHCI, MuleSoft, GitHub Pages), then branch protection.
- **Inputs:** none; consumes `scripts/projectInitCheck.sh` output. **Requires the Atlassian MCP** (`confluence_get_page` / `confluence_update_page`, page ID `305430530`).
- **Outputs:** **writes outside the repo** — updates a Confluence page (line 57). Also renames/edits `e2e/` placeholder files, updates `.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md`, and edits `browserstack.yml` (Tier 1 — gated on a `gh` identity check, lines 92–96).
- **Invokes:** `bash scripts/projectInitCheck.sh`, `gh api .../branches/release%2F*/protection` (proposed, not run — line 132).
- **Callable sub-step:** ❌ No. The only skill with side effects outside the repo.

### Planning & safety

**`feature-spec`** — `.claude/skills/feature-spec/SKILL.md`
> `description: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.`

- **Does:** Phase 1 one-question-at-a-time clarification against 8 fixed questions (lines 20–28); Phase 2 spawns **three parallel research agents** (A: reads `.claude/registry/{components,hooks,utils}.md` with a `find` fallback; B: nearest-pattern scan under `overrides/app/`; C: upstream scan of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` with a Take/Override/Skip recommendation); Phase 3 sprint check; Phase 4 spec.
- **Inputs:** a plain-English feature description. Note the body does **not** use `$ARGUMENTS` — it says "Read the feature description the user has provided" (line 13), even though README documents `/feature-spec <description>`. Reads `.docs/prd/`, `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`, `projectState.md`.
- **Outputs:** a markdown spec **in-conversation, not a file** — new-files table, existing-files+tier table, copy-first override table, hooks table, API shape, integration touchpoints, acceptance criteria, a **ready-to-paste scoped Claude Code prompt** (line 123, described at line 146 as "the primary deliverable"), and a PR checklist.
- **Invokes:** nothing directly; its checklist references `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`, `/code-quality`.
- **Callable sub-step:** ✅ **Yes** — the natural pre-build step, and its output prompt is a clean handoff into your build step.

**`scope-check`** — `.claude/skills/scope-check/SKILL.md`
> `description: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.`

- **Does:** predicts every file a prompt would touch (including drift via refactor-upward and shared imports), tiers each, assesses four named risk questions, verdicts ✅ SAFE / ⚠️ RISKY / 🚫 BLOCKED, then rewrites risky prompts with explicit paths + "Do not modify any other files".
- **Inputs:** `$ARGUMENTS` = the proposed prompt text (line 8). Reads `frozenFiles.md`, `protectedFiles.md`, `squadA.md`, `squadB.md`.
- **Outputs:** compact table + verdict paragraph + rewritten prompt in a code block. No files.
- **Invokes:** nothing.
- **Callable sub-step:** ✅ **Yes — highest value.** This is the one to wrap around any prompt your workflow is about to execute.

**`audit-tier`** — `.claude/skills/audit-tier/SKILL.md`
> `description: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.`

- **Does:** 5-part output — Tier (1–4), Owner, "Can Claude Code modify it?", import blast radius, and a specific next action.
- **Inputs:** `$ARGUMENTS` = a path (line 8).
- **Outputs:** report only.
- **Invokes:** an inline blast-radius command (lines 34–37): greps `overrides/app` for the basename, excludes `.test.`/`.stories.`, `wc -l`; **>5 = high blast radius**.
- **Callable sub-step:** ✅ **Yes** — cheapest per-file gate; good inner loop inside a larger pre-build check.

### Development

**`new-component`** — `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md`
> `description: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.`

- **Does:** reads a nearby existing component for style, then creates `index.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx` (with a decision gate on whether a story is needed at all), optional `index.test.ts`, optional `types.ts`.
- **Inputs:** `$ARGUMENTS` = component name (line 8). Reads `conventions.md`, `components.md`, `css.md`.
- **Outputs:** **writes new files.** Reports created paths, the import line, a wiring note, and tsc confirmation.
- **Invokes:** `npx tsc --noEmit` (line 54).
- **Hard constraint worth reusing:** line 58 — *"Do not modify any existing files (no auto-wiring into routes, parents, or the theme registry)."*
- **Callable sub-step:** ✅ **Yes** — during build.

### Quality & review

**`code-quality`** — `.claude/skills/code-quality/SKILL.md`
> `description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.`

- **Does:** four independent agents run **in parallel when >5 files**, sequentially otherwise — A naming/structure, B import analysis (circular, tier-jumping, later-sprint, `../../../..` depth), C TypeScript coverage, D test & story coverage (with an explicit rule at lines 95–101 that a `play` function elsewhere does *not* substitute for a component's own test).
- **Inputs:** optional path/dir. **Default with no argument: `git diff --name-only main`** (lines 15, 17). Excludes tests, stories, registry files.
- **Outputs:** a single prioritised 🔴/🟡/🔵 report (template at lines 123–142). Line 146: *"Do not modify any files — report only."*
- **Invokes:** `npx tsc --noEmit`, run **once for the whole branch, not per file** (line 86).
- **Callable sub-step:** ✅ **Yes** — post-build / pre-PR.

**`pr-checklist`** — `.claude/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md`
> `description: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.`

- **Does:** step 1 **invokes `/code-quality`** on the branch diff and hoists must-fixes to the top; tiers every changed file; flags cross-squad PRs; emits a copy-paste PR body with a tier table, required pre-merge actions, CodeRabbit gates, and a test checklist.
- **Inputs:** none. Uses **`git diff --name-only develop`** (lines 11, 13).
- **Outputs:** PR description markdown in-conversation. Nothing is posted to GitHub.
- **Invokes:** `/code-quality`; checklist references `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test`. Line 58 explicitly forbids Claude starting the dev server.
- **Callable sub-step:** ✅ **Yes** — before opening a PR. ⚠️ **It already calls `code-quality`** — calling both from your workflow doubles the audit.

**`code-review`** (symlink) — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.agents/skills/code-review/SKILL.md`
> `description: "AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security)."`
> (also carries `metadata: version: "0.1.0"` — the only skill with metadata)

- **Does:** prerequisite check (`coderabbit --version`, `coderabbit auth status`), runs `coderabbit review --agent`, groups findings Critical/Warning/Info, builds a task list, then an autonomous **fix loop**: implement → review → fix → re-review until only info-level remains.
- **Inputs:** none required. Optional scope: `-t all|committed|uncommitted`, `--base <branch>`, `--base-commit <sha>`, `--dir <path>`.
- **Outputs:** findings + task list; the fix loop **does edit files**.
- **Invokes:** external `coderabbit` / `cr` binary — **requires v0.4.0+** for `--agent`.
- **Callable sub-step:** ✅ **Yes, and effectively mandatory.** `AGENTS.md` Coding Task Workflow step 4 already requires `cr review --light --base develop` (or `main` on release/hotfix) before any non-trivial commit, and treats a missing/unauthenticated CLI as a **blocker**. Reuse this rather than reimplementing.

### QA

**`qa-generate`** — `.claude/skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md`
> `description: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.`

- **Does:** 6 phases. Phase 1 asks 6 story questions one at a time. Phase 2 writes the `.feature` and **hard-stops** (line 48). Phase 3 applies `# QA ANNOTATION:` corrections. Phase 4 generates the Playwright spec only after sign-off. Phase 5 proposes Page Object additions. Phase 6 summary.
- **Inputs:** no argument; asks Jira key, title, AC, squad, sprint, P0. Requires `e2e/` to exist (it does). Reads `e2e/features/README.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md`, `sprintScope.md`, and checks `.github/workflows/qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` allow-list groups.
- **Outputs:** **writes** `e2e/features/{area}/{KEY}_{desc}.feature`, then `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{KEY}_{desc}[.p0].spec.ts`.
- **Load-bearing rules:** every `test()` needs **both** `@area` and `@{JIRA-KEY}` tags (lines 86–95); optional `@zephyr:KEY` (lines 96–100); no `test.skip()` platform branching — use sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (lines 101–108); never on `develop`/`main` (line 143).
- **Callable sub-step:** ⚠️ **Partial** — human-gated by design, so it cannot run unattended end-to-end.

### Contentful

**`contentful-register-component`** — `.claude/skills/contentful-register-component/SKILL.md`
> `description: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.`
> **Also has `allowed-tools: Read, Edit, Bash` (line 4) — the only skill with a tool allowlist.**

- **Does:** moves the component under `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, adds `/** @cf-register */`, annotates props with `@cf Display Name[, control]` JSDoc tags, runs codegen. Definitions are generated from the TS `Props` type — never hand-written (line 100).
- **Inputs:** a component file path.
- **Outputs:** edits the component; the generator rewrites `experiences/definitions.ts`.

## 1. PR #56 — the token layer

### What changed in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`

Files touched (merge `2dfeb4d`): `colour.ts` (+83/−70), `typography.ts` (+123/−89), `zimmTokens.ts` (+133/−118), `spacing.ts` (+25/−13), `sizes.ts` (+4/−3), `index.ts` (+2/−2). Plus `theme/globalStyles.ts` (+6/−88) and the new governance doc `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (+178, new file).

Three structural moves:

1. **`zimmTokens.ts` became fully derived.** Before, every `--zimm-*` value was a hand-retyped literal (`'--zimm-color-grey-900': '#191919'`). After, it imports and references: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:6-12` imports `colors`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings`, `fontWeights`, `spacing`, `borderWidths`, `focusRingOffsets`, `iconSizes`, `actionSizes`, `grid`, `motion`, then maps them (`zimmTokens.ts:16` — `'--zimm-color-grey-black': colors.grey.black`).

3. **px → rem for anything that should scale** (WCAG 1.4.4). `spacing.ts:8-22` is entirely rem; px survives only for hairline geometry, and only as named tokens: `borderWidths` (`spacing.ts:26-28`) and `focusRingOffsets` (`spacing.ts:34-37`).

### The literal count

The 237 → 64 figure isn't stated verbatim in the commit or PR body. My independent count corroborates the magnitude: a hex/px/rem/em/rgba regex over code lines only (comments stripped) across `foundation/` gives **256 at `b6841a9`** (PR base) → **75 at `2dfeb4d`** — ~181 removed. ### Resulting token architecture

**Four layers, each a reference to the one below — never a copy.**

| Layer | File | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| Primitive | `foundation/colour.ts:6-37` | `grey`, `ivory`, `coral`, `green`, `orange`, `red`, `opacity` — plain `const`s, the only hex in the system |
| Semantic alias | `foundation/colour.ts:39-113` | `text`, `background`, `border`, `status`, `link`, `icon`, `action` — **read from the primitives** (`text.default: grey[900]`, line 61) |
| Scale primitives | `foundation/spacing.ts`, `typography.ts:6-34`, `sizes.ts`, `motion.ts`, `gridSystem.ts` | rem spacing scale, font sizes/line heights/letter spacings/weights, icon + action sizes |
| CSS-var registry | `foundation/zimmTokens.ts` | the flat `--zimm-*` map, derived from all of the above |

The stated rule is at `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:72` — *"The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy"*: "two values can't disagree if only one of them is ever typed."

**Naming scheme.** `--zimm-<domain>-<path>`:
- `--zimm-color-*` (`--zimm-color-grey-900`, `--zimm-color-text-default`, `--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover`)
- `--zimm-scale-*` — named steps (`3xs…7xl`) plus 15 numeric Handover aliases (`--zimm-scale-400`)
- `--zimm-font-size-* / -lineheight-* / -letterspacing-* / -weight-* / -family-*`
- `--zimm-icon-size-*`, `--zimm-size-action-*`, `--zimm-border-width-*`, `--zimm-focus-ring*`, `--zimm-grid-margin-*`, `--zimm-motion-*`

**How tokens get emitted — two separate channels, deliberately:**

- **CSS custom properties** → `overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:16-22` serialises `zimmTokens` into a raw Emotion `<Global>` `:root` block. It is **not** Chakra's `styles.global` — `zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:7-10` records why: Chakra's style processor mangles quoted font-family values, collapsing `"'Futura Round', 'Century Gothic', sans-serif"` to one family. Mounted at `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:160` (and in `.storybook/preview.tsx`, so app and Storybook cannot drift).
- **Chakra theme scales** → `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:51-64`. Only six foundations are registered: `borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space: spacing, textStyles`. `theme/index.ts:31-45` documents which are deliberately **not** registered and why — `fontSizes`, `transition` and `sizes` collide by key name with Chakra defaults used at ~199 base-template call sites (Chakra `sizes.lg` = 32rem vs `iconSizes.lg` = 20px).

### The rule for reaching for a value

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:12-37` — strict order:

1. `textStyle` prop for anything textual — never a raw `fontSize` (line 14)
2. Raw `var(--zimm-*)` for colour and spacing — **never a bare Chakra token string** like `color="text.default"` even though it resolves correctly (line 16)
3. The component's own theme config — `theme/components/<name>.ts` or a co-located `<name>.css.ts` (line 28)
4. `sx` for a one-off prop-system gap (line 35)
5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (line 36)

Line 39: **"Never: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file."**

### When a raw literal *is* acceptable

Three legitimate cases, all with evidence in-tree:

- **`foundation/` itself** — out of scan scope; a raw value there is the point (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:12-14`).
- **Genuinely context-relative units** — `em` for breakpoints. `theme/components/footerShared.ts:15-17` carries an explicit `audit-allow:` for exactly this: *"raw em is correct and permanent here, not a placeholder awaiting a token."*

2. `no typography property uses a bare scale key` (305) — `fontSize: '2xs'` reads Chakra's 10px, not Zimmermann's 14px; `lineHeight: '2xs'` resolves to nothing.

4. `no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale` (331) — **house style**, not a bug: `gap: 'xs'` resolves correctly but must be `var(--zimm-scale-xs)`.
5. `no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name` (347) — `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe named `Footer` *inherits* SFCC's `Footer` instead of replacing it. `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']`; everything else must be namespaced `Zimm*`.

**Documented blind spot** (`recipeGuards.test.ts:36-44`): these walk the registered recipe map only. They cannot see the same mistake as a JSX/`sx` prop — there is a live instance of failure mode 2 at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, emits nothing) that no test here reaches. `audit:tokens` is the broader-but-softer complement.

## 2. PR #59 — the component + CSS layer

### Component directory layout

```
overrides/app/components/footer/
  index.tsx                    ← Footer (presentational, named) + FooterContainer (default)
  index.stories.tsx            ← title: 'Layout/Footer'
  index.stories.content.ts     ← FOOTER_FIXTURE — Contentful-shaped, story-only
  index.test.tsx
  footer.css.ts                ← ZimmFooter shell recipe
  footerNavColumn/
    index.tsx
    index.test.tsx
    footerNavColumn.css.ts     ← ZimmFooterNavColumn
  bottomBar/
    index.tsx
    bottomBar.css.ts           ← ZimmFooterBottomBar
```

Rules governing this: `.claude/rules/conventions.md:81` (folder-per-component, `index.tsx`, camelCase for Zimmermann-authored / kebab-case for overrides), `.claude/rules/components.md:13` (named export matches folder name), `:15` (props type = `<ComponentName>Props`), `:121` (story required for anything exported from its folder; **not** required for a single-parent internal sub-component — which is exactly why `bottomBar/` has no story).

Test policy is stricter than "cover it transitively" — `.claude/rules/testing.md:9-24` explicitly says a component with real logic gets its own test file even when a hook test or a parent's `play` covers the same ground; resolve duplication by *scoping what it asserts* (mock the hook/child), not by skipping the file. `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` is named as the reference. `bottomBar` is exempt as "pure prop interpolation."

### Focused recipe vs shared style surface

**Focused, co-located recipe** — `footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`:
- Owns one component's own layout. Exports one recipe object (`ZimmFooterNavColumn`) with `parts: ['col','heading','list','listItem']` + `baseStyle`.
- **Composes only already-established tokens**: every value is `var(--zimm-scale-m)`, `var(--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey)`, `var(--zimm-font-family-body)`, `textStyle: 'navigation'`.
- Consumed by name, not by path: `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:7` `const ZIMM_FOOTER_NAV_COLUMN_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooterNavColumn'` → `useMultiStyleConfig(...)` at line 35.
- Comments carry the Figma node ID and the measurement reasoning (`footerNavColumn.css.ts:6-25` — a 15-line justification of the 160px cap, including the 13% fallback-font width delta).
- **CODEOWNERS routes it to the squads only** (`CODEOWNERS:186` — `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b`), last-match-wins deliberately overriding the Tier 2 `overrides/app/components/footer/` rule at `CODEOWNERS:87`.

**Shared style surface** — `theme/components/footerShared.ts`:
- Exports only values needed by **more than one** split-out file: `BP` (breakpoints) and `SIZE_COL_NAV`.
- It stays in `theme/components/` → **Tier 2, UI-designer gated** (`CODEOWNERS:117`).
- It is **not itself a recipe** — it's not in `theme/components/index.ts`'s `components` export.
- It's the one place allowed to import `foundation/` directly, with the reason stated at `footerShared.ts:13-14`: *"Media queries cannot consume var(), so this is the one deliberate exception."*
- The correctness reason for sharing is stated inline (`footerShared.ts:26-27`): `SIZE_COL_NAV` is used by both `footerNavColumn.css.ts` (column width) and `bottomBar.css.ts` (mobile legal-link width) — *"the two must match or the legal links stop lining up with the columns above them."*

**The decision rule**, stated at `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:239-244`:

> **Cross-file shared values** (a breakpoint or provisional size needed by more than one split-out file) go in a small shared module that stays in `theme/components/` — e.g. `footerShared.ts`… Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files.

Restated as a checkable test:

| Question | Answer → location |
|---|---|
| Used by exactly one component? | co-located `<name>.css.ts` beside it |
| Needed by ≥2 split-out files of the same feature? | a shared module in `theme/components/` (`footerShared.ts`) |
| Is it a **new raw design value** (authoring a token, not composing one)? | `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a still-gated `theme/components/*.ts` — `overrideStyling.md:212-215` |
| Is it app-wide, static, non-interactive, massively reused? | `theme/globalStyles.ts` `.zimm-*` class (`overrideStyling.md:104-106`) |

Registration is uniform regardless of file location: everything lands in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (19 recipes, lines 21-41), because *"Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an organisational choice with no runtime difference"* (`overrideStyling.md:201-205`).

### Other hard patterns PR #59 established

- **Namespace every new recipe `Zimm*`.** `overrideStyling.md:169-172` and enforced by guard 5. `theme/components/footer.ts` was deliberately named `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`.
- **Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand** (`overrideStyling.md:224-236`): ``[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' }``. The array form (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key at every step and fails guard 4. `footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` (line 38) and `linksInner` (line 71) are the reference.
- **Multipart vs single-part.** Multipart = plain object with `parts: [...]` + `baseStyle`, consumed via `useMultiStyleConfig` (11 of 13 co-located recipes). Single-part = `defineStyleConfig({baseStyle, variants, defaultProps})`, consumed via `useStyleConfig` — only `zimmButton.css.ts` and `zimmNavItem.css.ts`.
- **Presentational + container split in one file.** `footer/index.tsx` exports `Footer` (named, required `data` prop, fetches nothing, lines 68-133) and `FooterContainer` (default, owns the Contentful fetch, lines 172-217). The JSDoc at lines 158-171 explains why the seam exists at all: base `_app/index.jsx` renders `<Footer />` with no props, so there is no upstream container.
- **Fixtures live in a sibling `index.stories.content.ts`**, typed against the real Contentful type, and only ever feed the presentational export (`footer/index.stories.content.ts:1-9`).
- **Stories carry `play` for security-adjacent behaviour**, not just visuals — `footer/index.stories.tsx:28-40` asserts `target="_blank"` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` + the WCAG 3.2.5 accessible-name suffix.

## 3. atoms / molecules / organisms — as actually practised

### Current inventory

| Tier | Components |
|---|---|
| **atoms** (11) | zimmButton, zimmIcon, zimmLogo, zimmModal, zimmNavItem, zimmTextInput, zimmProductName, zimmProductPrice, zimmProductDescription, zimmProductModelInfo, zimmProductStyleCode |
| **molecules** (4) | zimmContactIconRow, zimmInputAction, zimmProductContent, zimmProductMeta |
| **organisms** (2) | zimmSubscribeModal, zimmSubscribeSection |

### What actually distinguishes them

The operative distinction is **what a component is allowed to import and own**, not size:

**Atom — imports no other ui-kit component; owns no cross-component state.**
- `zimmNavItem` (`atoms/zimmNavItem/index.tsx`) — one `<a>` or `<button>`. Imports nothing from ui-kits. Its whole visual contract (hover underline, focus ring, `light`/`inverse` variants) is in `zimmNavItem.css.ts`.
- `zimmProductStyleCode` (`atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx`) — renders one line, returns nothing when the value is absent. Single prop `value?: string`.
- `zimmModal` (`atoms/zimmModal/index.tsx`) — deliberately owns *no content*: portal + backdrop + accessible dialog panel, caller supplies children. That's what keeps it an atom despite being structurally involved.

**Molecule — composes ≥2 atoms; may own trivial local UI state; owns no business/domain state.**
- `zimmInputAction` (`molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx:1-5`) imports `ZimmTextInput` + `ZimmButton` + `ZimmIconType`. It holds one `useState` for a validation string (line 26) — presentation-local only. Notably it has **no `.css.ts`** at all; it borrows its children's recipes and adds a single inline `__css` on the form (line 60).
- `zimmContactIconRow` composes three `ZimmIcon`s into a labelled row; the JSDoc explicitly says *"nothing here is footer-specific"* — reusability is part of the tier claim.
- `zimmProductMeta` = `ZimmProductModelInfo` + `ZimmProductStyleCode` — the whole component is two atoms in design order.

**Organism — composes molecules/atoms **and** reaches outside itself: a custom hook, app-wide context, or another organism.**
- `zimmSubscribeSection` (`organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:1-6`) is the clearest case. It imports `ZimmInputAction` (molecule) + `ZimmSubscribeModal` (organism) **and** `useSubscribeSection` (a hook owning a 4-state machine: idle/success/unavailable/error) **and** `useUiCopy` (app-wide Contentful-backed context). It has its own `index.test.tsx`.
- `zimmSubscribeModal` — composes `ZimmModal` + form fields into a complete, self-contained feature unit with a defined job.

Rough correlate: atoms have 1-3 props; organisms are the tier that gets `index.test.tsx` and a hook.

### Is it documented?

**No — it is purely implied by placement, plus two soft conventions.** I searched every `.md`, `.ts`, `.tsx` outside `node_modules`: there is **no file anywhere that defines atom vs molecule vs organism.** Neither `.claude/rules/components.md`, `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md`, nor `.docs/architecture.md` mentions the words. The only references are incidental (`.claude/rules/testing.md:16` cites an organism's test as an example; `overrideStyling.md:201`, `:249` cite paths).

The two conventions that *do* carry the signal:

1. **JSDoc first word.** Every ui-kit component's docblock opens `Atom — …` / `Molecule — …` (e.g. `atoms/zimmNavItem/index.tsx:28`, `molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx:24`, `molecules/zimmProductContent/index.tsx:39`). The two organisms are the inconsistency: neither says "Organism —"; `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:30` says *"Newsletter sign-up organism"* mid-sentence.
2. **`.claude/registry/components.md`** — auto-generated by `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`, mirrors those JSDoc first lines into a table (lines 85-101). It surfaces the tier but doesn't define it.

**Critically: the folder tier is orthogonal to the Storybook category.** `.claude/rules/components.md:131` defines `Foundation/ Elements/ Layout/ Commerce/ Forms/ Pages/ Contentful/` — a *domain* taxonomy. Atoms land in both `Elements/` (zimmButton, zimmNavItem, zimmModal) and `Commerce/` (zimmProductPrice, zimmProductName); molecules land in `Elements/` (zimmContactIconRow), `Forms/` (zimmInputAction) and `Commerce/` (zimmProductMeta); organisms land in `Forms/`. A skill must not conflate the two.

**Gap worth flagging for the skill:** these are the two rules most likely to be silently violated, because nothing checks them. A workflow skill could mechanically enforce (a) JSDoc starts with `Atom —`/`Molecule —`/`Organism —` matching the parent folder, and (b) an atom's `index.tsx` contains no import from `../../molecules/` or `../../organisms/`.

## 4. Override vs. custom — the decision

### The documented rule (and its staleness)

`.docs/architecture.md:127-130`:

> - **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
> - **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.

**`overrides/app/components/custom/` does not exist.** The directory listing is `_app-config, contentful, footer, foundation, header, icons, pageContainer, product-view, ui-kits, uiCopyProvider`. PR #59 established `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/` as the real home for brand-new components, and `.docs/architecture.md:130` was never updated. `CODEOWNERS:173-176` now describes `ui-kits/` as *"the shared design-system layer consumed by both squads' component overrides"* — i.e. the custom tier, under a different name. **A workflow skill should encode `ui-kits/`, and flag architecture.md:130 as stale.**

### The actual decision procedure

**Does a base file exist at the mirrored path in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/…`?**

**Yes → override.** Then the **Copy-first rule** is mandatory and blocking (`AGENTS.md` > Rules > Copy-first; `.docs/architecture.md:120-125`):
1. Copy the file to the mirrored path in `overrides/`
2. Convert `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`, replace `PropTypes` with TS types, no `as any` / `@ts-ignore`
3. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] …')` to prove the override is rendering
5. **Stop and present to the user** before any functional change

Filename discipline: an override keeps the base kebab-case name (`product-tile/index.tsx`); Zimmermann-authored is camelCase (`.claude/rules/conventions.md:76-79`).

**No → custom**, under `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<zimmComponentName>/`.

### Two extra constraints that are actually the sharp edges

**a) If the base component is used internally by SFCC's own components, the default export must stay a faithful port.** `overrideStyling.md:173-186`: check with `grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`. If it's an internal dependency, keep the default export API-compatible and put brand styling behind a named export (`product-tile`'s `CardBaseline` + default) or, preferably now, a theme recipe.

**b) Import an already-overridden component by *relative* path, never the base path.** `overrideStyling.md:150-166`. The `ccExtensibility` resolver only runs in the real webpack build — `.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it. A base-path import ships correctly but **silently renders the unstyled base SFCC component in Storybook and Vitest**. A known unfixed instance is named: `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import.

### Evidence from the two PRs

- **PR #59 did both, on the same feature.** `footer/index.tsx` is an *override* (mirrors base `app/components/footer`, keeps kebab-case, default export is what SFCC renders) — while its six new building blocks are *custom* (`ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput`, `ui-kits/molecules/zimmInputAction`). The dividing line is exactly "does a base file exist at that path."
- **PR #59 also relocated a recipe across the boundary**: `theme/components/button.ts` (deleted, −119) → `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` (+251). The governance consequence is flagged, unresolved, in `overrideStyling.md:218-226`: the move dropped those provisional constants out of the designer's Tier 2 gate, and the doc says explicitly *"Whether `zimmButton.css.ts` should be re-gated is an open governance question, not a doc fix, and is deliberately left open here."*
- **PR #56's scoping decision** is the other direction: `link.ts` was cut from the PR because *"the component doesn't exist on `develop` yet"* — a theme recipe is not created ahead of the component it styles.

## 5. Contentful integration

There are **two entirely separate paths**, and conflating them is the main failure mode.

### Path A — Studio Experiences (drag-and-drop page builder)

Directory: `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`. Only files here are processed.

Developer steps (`.claude/skills/contentful-register-component/SKILL.md`, and `scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs:1-22`):

1. Put the component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/<name>.tsx`
2. Add `/** @cf-register */` immediately before the component's `const` declaration
3. Annotate each exposed prop: `/** @cf Display Name */` or `/** @cf Display Name, control */`
4. `npm run generate:contentful` → rewrites `experiences/definitions.ts` (never hand-edited)
5. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run generate:contentful:check` (exits 0 if in sync)

Mechanics: ts-morph AST walk. Controls are `shortText | longText | select | toggle | number | media` (`generateDefinitions.mjs:43-51`). Inference: `string→shortText`, `boolean→toggle`, `number→number`, string-literal union→`select`. Auto-skipped: `on*` handlers and `children` (emits `children: true`). Component `id` = kebab-case of the filename; `name` = Title Case. **Untagged non-handler props fail loudly.** The pre-commit hook auto-runs the generator when an `experiences/*.tsx` file is staged (`scripts/hooks/pre-commit:127-164`).

**Current state: empty.** `experiences/definitions.ts` calls `defineComponents([])` — PR #59 deleted `hotspotMarker.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx`, `shoppableImage.tsx` (unused Hardi-era scaffolding). The file's header (lines 3-8) documents the hand-restored empty state because the generator refuses to write output when zero components are found. `overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts` is now an empty file.

### Path B — content-model-driven components (what PR #59 actually used)

This is the live path. **Four steps:**

**1. Define the content type in code** — `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js`, one file per type, sole source of truth for fields including `localized`/`required`/`validations`. Existing: `footerConfig.js`, `footerNavGroup.js`, `link.js`, `region.js`, `image.js`, `uiCopy.js`. Then:
```
npm run sync:contentful                       # builds the org-scoped Environment Template
npm run install:contentful -- --target dev    # per environment in the promotion chain
```
(`.docs/architecture.md:160-196`; `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` > Contentful Schema Definitions — Tier 2, Integration/SI owned. Field deletion is opt-in via `--delete-deleted-fields`, off by default.)

**2. Mirror the shape in TypeScript** — `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`. Types present: `RegionEntry` (:64), `LinkEntry` (:86), `FooterNavGroupEntry` (:102), `FooterConfigEntry` (:121), `UiCopyEntry` (:158). `architecture.md:194` states the rule: *"The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`."*

**3. Register the ID** — `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts`, `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`: `region, link, footerNavGroup, footerConfig, uiCopy`. This file also owns per-tier environment mapping (`dev/test/sit/staging/uat/master`) and locale→site mapping.

**4. Fetch in a container, render in a presentational component.** `FooterContainer` (`footer/index.tsx:172-217`) uses `useContentfulClient()` → `client.getEntries({content_type: 'footerConfig', include: FOOTER_INCLUDE_DEPTH})` → `pickMostSpecificByRegion` → `scopeToRegion`. The presentational `Footer` takes `data: FooterConfigEntry` as a required prop and fetches nothing.

### Content types involved and their roles

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `footerConfig` | Root entry — subscribe copy, `navGroups[]`, `legalLinks[]`, `copyrightOwner`, `phoneHref`/`whatsAppHref`/`emailHref`, `regions[]` |
| `footerNavGroup` | One nav column — heading, `links[]`, `showContactChannels` |
| `link` | `{label, href, regions[]}` — the reusable, region-scopable link |
| `region` | `{siteId, label, locale}` — maps a Contentful entry to an SFCC site |
| `uiCopy` | One entry per UI string: `{title, key (unique, non-localized), value (localized), description}` |

### Three project-specific gotchas a skill should encode

1. **`include` depth is load-bearing and fails hard.** `footer/index.tsx:17-27`: the footer model is exactly three levels (`footerConfig → navGroups → links → regions`). At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved link stubs with no `fields`, `region.fields.siteId` throws, `.catch` swallows it, and **the entire footer renders nothing.** Note `useContentful.ts` hardcodes 2 for asset resolution — a different concern, not a house default.

2. **Region scoping is applied in code, not by Contentful.** `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts` — `filterByRegion` (inclusive, for arrays where multiple regional entries coexist) vs `pickMostSpecificByRegion` (precedence: fewer `regions` = more specific; unscoped sorts last, `specificity()` returns `Infinity`).

3. **Failure behaviour is deliberately split by content kind.** Structural content fails closed — `FooterContainer` returns `null` rather than substitute placeholder copy (`footer/index.tsx:164-168`). Microcopy fails open — `UiCopyProvider` (`uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:30-33`) states: *"unlike structural content… losing a button label or a status message to a Contentful outage should never blank a control."*

The `uiCopy` pattern is worth calling out as its own reusable primitive: one bulk CDA call per locale for the whole app (`UiCopyProvider`, mounted at `_app-config/index.tsx:161`), assembled into a key→value `Map`, exposed as `t(key, fallback)`. `useUiCopy` degrades to `FALLBACK_ONLY` with no Provider (`hooks/useUiCopy.ts:19-22, :37`), which is why `.claude/rules/components.md:73-88` grants it an explicit exception to the no-data-fetching-in-leaves rule — and why the same paragraph warns that `useIntl` does **not** share that property (it throws, and its Provider sits in base SFCC `_app`, a strictly narrower subtree than `_app-config`).

| 1 | No raw hex/px/rem/em in `components/**` or `theme/components/**` | `overrideStyling.md:39` | `npm run audit:tokens` — advisory, not in CI |

## 1. PR #56 — the token layer

### What changed in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`

Files touched (merge `2dfeb4d`): `colour.ts` (+83/−70), `typography.ts` (+123/−89), `zimmTokens.ts` (+133/−118), `spacing.ts` (+25/−13), `sizes.ts` (+4/−3), `index.ts` (+2/−2). Plus `theme/globalStyles.ts` (+6/−88) and the new governance doc `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (+178, new file).

Three structural moves:

1. **`zimmTokens.ts` became fully derived.** Before, every `--zimm-*` value was a hand-retyped literal (`'--zimm-color-grey-900': '#191919'`). After, it imports and references: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:6-12` imports `colors`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings`, `fontWeights`, `spacing`, `borderWidths`, `focusRingOffsets`, `iconSizes`, `actionSizes`, `grid`, `motion`, then maps them (`zimmTokens.ts:16` — `'--zimm-color-grey-black': colors.grey.black`).
2. **`typography.ts` gained a primitive scale layer** it previously lacked — `fontSizes` / `lineHeights` / `letterSpacings` / `fontWeights` (`typography.ts:6-34`), deduplicated out of the 22 named `textStyles` below them (`typography.ts:38-239`).
3. **px → rem for anything that should scale** (WCAG 1.4.4). `spacing.ts:8-22` is entirely rem; px survives only for hairline geometry, and only as named tokens: `borderWidths` (`spacing.ts:26-28`) and `focusRingOffsets` (`spacing.ts:34-37`).

### The literal count

The 237 → 64 figure isn't stated verbatim in the commit or PR body. My independent count corroborates the magnitude: a hex/px/rem/em/rgba regex over code lines only (comments stripped) across `foundation/` gives **256 at `b6841a9`** (PR base) → **75 at `2dfeb4d`** — ~181 removed. ### Resulting token architecture

**Four layers, each a reference to the one below — never a copy.**

| Layer | File | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| Primitive | `foundation/colour.ts:6-37` | `grey`, `ivory`, `coral`, `green`, `orange`, `red`, `opacity` — plain `const`s, the only hex in the system |
| Semantic alias | `foundation/colour.ts:39-113` | `text`, `background`, `border`, `status`, `link`, `icon`, `action` — **read from the primitives** (`text.default: grey[900]`, line 61) |
| Scale primitives | `foundation/spacing.ts`, `typography.ts:6-34`, `sizes.ts`, `motion.ts`, `gridSystem.ts` | rem spacing scale, font sizes/line heights/letter spacings/weights, icon + action sizes |
| CSS-var registry | `foundation/zimmTokens.ts` | the flat `--zimm-*` map, derived from all of the above |

The stated rule is at `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:72` — *"The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy"*: "two values can't disagree if only one of them is ever typed."

**Naming scheme.** `--zimm-<domain>-<path>`:
- `--zimm-color-*` (`--zimm-color-grey-900`, `--zimm-color-text-default`, `--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover`)
- `--zimm-scale-*` — named steps (`3xs…7xl`) plus 15 numeric Handover aliases (`--zimm-scale-400`)
- `--zimm-font-size-* / -lineheight-* / -letterspacing-* / -weight-* / -family-*`
- `--zimm-icon-size-*`, `--zimm-size-action-*`, `--zimm-border-width-*`, `--zimm-focus-ring*`, `--zimm-grid-margin-*`, `--zimm-motion-*`

**How tokens get emitted — two separate channels, deliberately:**

- **CSS custom properties** → `overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:16-22` serialises `zimmTokens` into a raw Emotion `<Global>` `:root` block. It is **not** Chakra's `styles.global` — `zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:7-10` records why: Chakra's style processor mangles quoted font-family values, collapsing `"'Futura Round', 'Century Gothic', sans-serif"` to one family. Mounted at `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:160` (and in `.storybook/preview.tsx`, so app and Storybook cannot drift).
- **Chakra theme scales** → `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:51-64`. Only six foundations are registered: `borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space: spacing, textStyles`. `theme/index.ts:31-45` documents which are deliberately **not** registered and why — `fontSizes`, `transition` and `sizes` collide by key name with Chakra defaults used at ~199 base-template call sites (Chakra `sizes.lg` = 32rem vs `iconSizes.lg` = 20px).

### The rule for reaching for a value

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:12-37` — strict order:

1. `textStyle` prop for anything textual — never a raw `fontSize` (line 14)
2. Raw `var(--zimm-*)` for colour and spacing — **never a bare Chakra token string** like `color="text.default"` even though it resolves correctly (line 16)
3. The component's own theme config — `theme/components/<name>.ts` or a co-located `<name>.css.ts` (line 28)
4. `sx` for a one-off prop-system gap (line 35)
5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (line 36)

Line 39: **"Never: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file."**

### When a raw literal *is* acceptable

Three legitimate cases, all with evidence in-tree:

- **`foundation/` itself** — out of scan scope; a raw value there is the point (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:12-14`).
- **Genuinely context-relative units** — `em` for breakpoints. `theme/components/footerShared.ts:15-17` carries an explicit `audit-allow:` for exactly this: *"raw em is correct and permanent here, not a placeholder awaiting a token."*
- **A value with no token yet, pending designer sign-off** — must be a **named constant with an explanatory comment**, never an inline literal. Canonical examples: `zimmButton.css.ts:202-207` (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG = '50px'`, `BTN_HEIGHT_SM`, `BTN_PADDING_Y`), `footer.css.ts:3-13` (`SPACE_SECTION`, `SIZE_COL_SUB`, `SIZE_COL_MAP`, `COLOUR_HALF_INV`), `zimmNavItem.css.ts:2-11` (`NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y = '4.5px'`).

### `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — what it actually enforces

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Command | `npm run audit:tokens` (`package.json:76`) |
| Scan roots | `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` (line 54) |
| Extensions | `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.scss` (line 55) |
| Excluded files | `*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`, `*.stories.tsx` (lines 61-62) |
| Excluded path | `theme/foundation/` — not under either root (lines 12-14) |
| Patterns | `HEX_RE = /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/g` (line 57); `UNIT_RE = /\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:rem|em|px)\b/g` (line 58) |
| Comment handling | `stripComments()` (lines 83-104) removes `//` and `/* */` so a Figma hex quoted in prose isn't flagged. `//` is not treated as a comment when preceded by `:` — otherwise `'https://wa.me/…'` truncates the line |
| Exit code | `1` if any unacknowledged finding (line 167) |
| CI status | **Not wired into CI** (lines 42-43, and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:231-238`). Advisory only |

**The escape hatch.** `EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE = /provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow/i` (line 59). A match is downgraded from failure → *acknowledged exception* (printed, but doesn't affect exit code) when **the contiguous non-blank block of lines ending at the match** contains one of those words (lines 119-122).

Two design details worth encoding in a skill:
- The context window is "up to the nearest blank line or file start", **not a fixed N lines** (lines 29-34). This is because real exception comments in this repo are multi-line shared blocks (`footer.css.ts`'s four constants share one comment) or wrap the marker across a line break.
- There is **no separate allow-list file** — the explanatory comment *is* the allow-list entry (lines 25-27), specifically to avoid a second list that drifts.

### The second, *hard* gate: `recipeGuards.test.ts`

`overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` runs on every `npm run test` and **fails the build**. Five guards (bodies at lines 286-364):

1. `no sizing property uses a bare spacing-scale key` (295) — `width: 'xl'` reads Chakra `sizes.xl` (36rem), not `space.xl`. Shipped a 576px icon and collapsed the footer.
2. `no typography property uses a bare scale key` (305) — `fontSize: '2xs'` reads Chakra's 10px, not Zimmermann's 14px; `lineHeight: '2xs'` resolves to nothing.
3. `no compound shorthand contains a bare scale key` (315) — `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and the browser drops it.
4. `no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale` (331) — **house style**, not a bug: `gap: 'xs'` resolves correctly but must be `var(--zimm-scale-xs)`.
5. `no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name` (347) — `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe named `Footer` *inherits* SFCC's `Footer` instead of replacing it. `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']`; everything else must be namespaced `Zimm*`.

**Documented blind spot** (`recipeGuards.test.ts:36-44`): these walk the registered recipe map only. They cannot see the same mistake as a JSX/`sx` prop — there is a live instance of failure mode 2 at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, emits nothing) that no test here reaches. `audit:tokens` is the broader-but-softer complement.

## 2. PR #59 — the component + CSS layer

### Component directory layout

```
overrides/app/components/footer/
  index.tsx                    ← Footer (presentational, named) + FooterContainer (default)
  index.stories.tsx            ← title: 'Layout/Footer'
  index.stories.content.ts     ← FOOTER_FIXTURE — Contentful-shaped, story-only
  index.test.tsx
  footer.css.ts                ← ZimmFooter shell recipe
  footerNavColumn/
    index.tsx
    index.test.tsx
    footerNavColumn.css.ts     ← ZimmFooterNavColumn
  bottomBar/
    index.tsx
    bottomBar.css.ts           ← ZimmFooterBottomBar
```

Rules governing this: `.claude/rules/conventions.md:81` (folder-per-component, `index.tsx`, camelCase for Zimmermann-authored / kebab-case for overrides), `.claude/rules/components.md:13` (named export matches folder name), `:15` (props type = `<ComponentName>Props`), `:121` (story required for anything exported from its folder; **not** required for a single-parent internal sub-component — which is exactly why `bottomBar/` has no story).

Test policy is stricter than "cover it transitively" — `.claude/rules/testing.md:9-24` explicitly says a component with real logic gets its own test file even when a hook test or a parent's `play` covers the same ground; resolve duplication by *scoping what it asserts* (mock the hook/child), not by skipping the file. `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` is named as the reference. `bottomBar` is exempt as "pure prop interpolation."

### Focused recipe vs shared style surface

**Focused, co-located recipe** — `footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`:
- Owns one component's own layout. Exports one recipe object (`ZimmFooterNavColumn`) with `parts: ['col','heading','list','listItem']` + `baseStyle`.
- **Composes only already-established tokens**: every value is `var(--zimm-scale-m)`, `var(--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey)`, `var(--zimm-font-family-body)`, `textStyle: 'navigation'`.
- Consumed by name, not by path: `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:7` `const ZIMM_FOOTER_NAV_COLUMN_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooterNavColumn'` → `useMultiStyleConfig(...)` at line 35.
- Comments carry the Figma node ID and the measurement reasoning (`footerNavColumn.css.ts:6-25` — a 15-line justification of the 160px cap, including the 13% fallback-font width delta).
- **CODEOWNERS routes it to the squads only** (`CODEOWNERS:186` — `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b`), last-match-wins deliberately overriding the Tier 2 `overrides/app/components/footer/` rule at `CODEOWNERS:87`.

**Shared style surface** — `theme/components/footerShared.ts`:
- Exports only values needed by **more than one** split-out file: `BP` (breakpoints) and `SIZE_COL_NAV`.
- It stays in `theme/components/` → **Tier 2, UI-designer gated** (`CODEOWNERS:117`).
- It is **not itself a recipe** — it's not in `theme/components/index.ts`'s `components` export.
- It's the one place allowed to import `foundation/` directly, with the reason stated at `footerShared.ts:13-14`: *"Media queries cannot consume var(), so this is the one deliberate exception."*
- The correctness reason for sharing is stated inline (`footerShared.ts:26-27`): `SIZE_COL_NAV` is used by both `footerNavColumn.css.ts` (column width) and `bottomBar.css.ts` (mobile legal-link width) — *"the two must match or the legal links stop lining up with the columns above them."*

**The decision rule**, stated at `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:239-244`:

> **Cross-file shared values** (a breakpoint or provisional size needed by more than one split-out file) go in a small shared module that stays in `theme/components/` — e.g. `footerShared.ts`… Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files.

Restated as a checkable test:

| Question | Answer → location |
|---|---|
| Used by exactly one component? | co-located `<name>.css.ts` beside it |
| Needed by ≥2 split-out files of the same feature? | a shared module in `theme/components/` (`footerShared.ts`) |
| Is it a **new raw design value** (authoring a token, not composing one)? | `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a still-gated `theme/components/*.ts` — `overrideStyling.md:212-215` |
| Is it app-wide, static, non-interactive, massively reused? | `theme/globalStyles.ts` `.zimm-*` class (`overrideStyling.md:104-106`) |

Registration is uniform regardless of file location: everything lands in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (19 recipes, lines 21-41), because *"Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an organisational choice with no runtime difference"* (`overrideStyling.md:201-205`).

### Other hard patterns PR #59 established

- **Namespace every new recipe `Zimm*`.** `overrideStyling.md:169-172` and enforced by guard 5. `theme/components/footer.ts` was deliberately named `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`.
- **Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand** (`overrideStyling.md:224-236`): ``[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' }``. The array form (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key at every step and fails guard 4. `footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` (line 38) and `linksInner` (line 71) are the reference.
- **Multipart vs single-part.** Multipart = plain object with `parts: [...]` + `baseStyle`, consumed via `useMultiStyleConfig` (11 of 13 co-located recipes). Single-part = `defineStyleConfig({baseStyle, variants, defaultProps})`, consumed via `useStyleConfig` — only `zimmButton.css.ts` and `zimmNavItem.css.ts`.
- **Presentational + container split in one file.** `footer/index.tsx` exports `Footer` (named, required `data` prop, fetches nothing, lines 68-133) and `FooterContainer` (default, owns the Contentful fetch, lines 172-217). The JSDoc at lines 158-171 explains why the seam exists at all: base `_app/index.jsx` renders `<Footer />` with no props, so there is no upstream container.
- **Fixtures live in a sibling `index.stories.content.ts`**, typed against the real Contentful type, and only ever feed the presentational export (`footer/index.stories.content.ts:1-9`).
- **Stories carry `play` for security-adjacent behaviour**, not just visuals — `footer/index.stories.tsx:28-40` asserts `target="_blank"` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` + the WCAG 3.2.5 accessible-name suffix.
