## 7. State of the styling rule — `var(--zimm-*)`

**The rule did reverse, and it reversed inside PR #59 — not in #56.** Verified by `git show e1732a3:.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (PR #56's head), which read:

> ```
> 2. **Semantic colour/spacing token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
>    `spacing="m"`, `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`. These resolve through
>    `theme.colors`/`theme.space` (both registered — see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment
>    for which foundation scales are and aren't registered, and why).
> ```

The reversal commits are `9d5f89c refactor(theme): require var(--zimm-*) over bare Chakra token keys in overrides` and `49a95b9 docs(rules): stop instructing the bare token key the guard now blocks`.

### Current direction on `develop` — `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:14-27`, verbatim

> ```
> 1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
>    All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
> 2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
>    `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
>    token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
>    ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
>    which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
>    is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
>    unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
>    `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
>    enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
>    override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
>    registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
>    that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
> ```

And `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:138-145`:

> ```
> When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
> `iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
> — `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
> `marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
> form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
> used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
> `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
> so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.
> ```

### Recipe or JSX? The rule text and the code disagree — read this carefully

The **rule text is agnostic on location**: hierarchy point 2's examples are written as **JSX props** (`color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`), so on a literal reading `var(--zimm-*)` is permitted in JSX. Point 2 forbids the *bare key*, not the *JSX location*.

But the surrounding rules push everything into the recipe. `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, "One canonical styling surface per component type", verbatim:

> ```
> Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
> either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
> beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
> `<Link>` variant, etc.).
> ```

**The de-facto convention in code is overwhelmingly "recipe", and it is near-absolute.** Verified by grep across `overrides/app/components`:
- **17 `.css.ts` recipe files** contain `var(--zimm-*)`
- **exactly 1 component `.tsx`** contains it (excluding stories/tests): `overrides/app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44` and `:62` — and both are inside a `__css={{ ...styles.part, ...conditional }}` spread, i.e. a conditional the recipe genuinely cannot express, not ordinary styling.

Every `zimmProduct*` component applies styling **only** via `__css={styles.part}` with zero inline token values. So: **put `var(--zimm-*)` in the co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipe.** Reach for a JSX `__css` spread only for a genuinely conditional value, following `footerNavColumn`'s shape.

One caveat the rule states explicitly: the guard *"walks the registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop… apply the same discipline there by hand."* The JSX half is unenforced. Note also `textStyle` stays a bare key — `.claude/rules/css.md` says there is no `var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite expansion.

## 2. The nearest existing pattern

The true nearest precedent is **PR #64 (SFCC-89)**, which created the whole `zimmProduct*` family, and **PR #68 (SFCC-194)**, which extended `zimmProductPrice`. (Both are more directly in-kind than #59/#56.)

### Exemplar file list — mirror this exactly
`zimmProductStyleCode` is the cleanest complete four-file unit:
```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/index.stories.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/index.test.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts
```
plus one line added to `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (import + `components` object key).

### `index.tsx` shape (verified against `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx` and `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx`)
- Recipe key hoisted to a module const: `const ZIMM_PRODUCT_STYLE_CODE_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductStyleCode';` (`:5`)
- `useMultiStyleConfig(KEY, {...})` for multipart, `useStyleConfig(KEY, {})` for single-part (`zimmProductContent/index.tsx:53`)
- Styling applied via `<chakra.x __css={styles.part}>` — **never** `sx`/style props
- Props type `type Zimm<Name>Props = {...}` co-located at top, every field JSDoc'd
- **Hooks above any early return** — `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:53-55` comments this explicitly (`rules-of-hooks`)
- Renders `null` when it has nothing to show, so callers can place it unconditionally
- Labels come from `react-intl` `intl.formatMessage`, **not** `useUiCopy` and not literals — rationale at `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:34-39` (`useContentful.ts` sends no `locale`, so `uiCopy` would serve the space default to all 8 storefronts)
- Use `const intl = useIntl()` then `intl.formatMessage(...)`; do **not** destructure (`@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`) — `:49-51`
- `data-testid` on the root

### `<name>.css.ts` recipe shape (`zimmProductPrice.css.ts`)
- `import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';`
- `export const ZimmProductPrice = { parts: [...], baseStyle: {...}, variants: {...}, defaultProps: {...} }`
- Every declared part must appear in `baseStyle`, even as `{}` stubs — `:26-31` explains why (Chakra gates variant resolution through the declared parts list)
- Each part object suffixed `satisfies SystemStyleObject`
- Colour/spacing as `var(--zimm-*)`; type as `textStyle` **in the recipe, not on the JSX element** (`:11-15`)

### Registration (`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`)
Import via the `app/` alias with `.css` and **no** `.ts` extension, then add the key:
```ts
import { ZimmProductPrice } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/zimmProductPrice.css';   // :15
export const components = { ..., ZimmProductPrice, ... };                                                 // :36
```

### Story (`zimmProductPrice/index.stories.tsx`)
`title: 'Commerce/Zimm<Name>'` (`:7`), a `Default` export, named exports for meaningful states only. A `play` is required where there is interactive behaviour — 17 story files already have one; `zimmProductContent/index.stories.tsx:74-108` is the reference (asserts child counts and computed `rowGap`).

### Test (`zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx`)
Scoped to the component's own contract; wraps renders in `IntlProvider` when `useIntl` is used (`:29-34`); asserts a11y attributes and text content, not internals.

### Two mechanical guards a new recipe must pass (`npm run test`)
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts:101` — declared `parts` must cover every part the sibling `index.tsx` reads off `styles.*`
- `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` — 6 guards, including `:331` (no bare token key on a registered scale) and `:347` (no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name)

| Piece | Base file at mirrored path? | SFCC's own components import it? | Call |
|---|---|---|---|
| `components/swatch-group/index.jsx` | **Yes** | **Yes — 2** (`product-tile:30`, `product-view:55`) | **Override, faithful port.** Default export must keep the full prop surface |
| `components/swatch-group/swatch.jsx` | **Yes** | **Yes — 2** (`product-tile:29`, `product-view:54`) | Same |
| `components/product-view/index.jsx` | **Yes — already overridden** | **Yes — 4** | Already a faithful port; extend via a render-slot, not a fork |
| `pages/product-detail/index.jsx` | **Yes — already overridden** | 1 internal + `routes.jsx:43` relative import (already solved in `overrides/app/routes.tsx:26-33`) | Already overridden |
| `components/product-tile/index.jsx` | **Yes** | Yes — 3 | Not overridden; **out of scope**, but it consumes swatch-group |
| `components/display-price/` | **Yes** | Yes — 6 | Not overridden; out of scope |
| `components/image-gallery/` | **Yes** | Yes — 2 | Not overridden. In scope *only* if PRD-062 (gallery updates on swatch select) is included |
| `hooks/use-variant.js`, `use-variation-attributes.js`, `use-variation-params.js`, `use-derived-product.js`, `use-controlled-variations.js` | **Yes, all** | Yes, via the **`hooks/index.js` barrel** (19 base importers) | **Do not override.** Reached through a barrel, so it resolves in the app build but **not** in Storybook/Vitest |
| A new `Zimm*` swatch component in `ui-kits/` | **No base equivalent** | n/a | **Custom** — the `zimmProduct*` pattern applies |

### The faithful-port constraint, concretely
Verified by reading both base files:
- `SwatchGroup` props (`index.jsx:29`): `ariaLabel, displayName, children, label = '', value, handleChange = noop`. **No `forwardRef`.** `useStyleConfig('SwatchGroup')` at `:31`. `role="radiogroup"` at `:94`. Arrow-key roving focus at `:54-64`. Injects `handleSelect`/`selected`/`isFocusable` into children via `React.cloneElement` at `:110-114`.
- `Swatch` props (`swatch.jsx:23-34`): `children, disabled, href, label, name, selected, isFocusable, value, handleSelect, variant = 'square'`. **No `forwardRef`.** `useMultiStyleConfig('SwatchGroup', {variant, disabled, selected})` at `:35` — **both components share the one `SwatchGroup` theme key.** Variants: `square` | `circle`.

### Two base behaviours worth planning around (verified)
1. **`disabled` is visual-only.** `swatch.jsx:35` feeds it to `useMultiStyleConfig` and it is never spread onto the `<Button>` — no `isDisabled`, no `aria-disabled`, no click guard (`:57-70`). An unorderable swatch still navigates and is not announced as disabled. That is a WCAG 2.2 AA gap you would inherit.
2. **Hover-select exists but not on the PDP.** `swatch.jsx:47-55` binds `onMouseEnter` at `lg`+ — but only when there is no `href` (`:69`: `{...(href ? {} : selectHandlers)}`). `use-variation-attributes.js:152-153` sets `href: null` only in *controlled* mode (the quick-view modals). On the PDP path `href` is a real URL, so swatches are `RouteLink`s and hover-select does **not** fire. This matters because `.docs/prd/pdp.md:19` says hover-preview is "**custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live**" — correct for the PDP, but the behaviour *is* live in the quick-view modals.

### The dormant trap you would create
The moment `overrides/app/components/swatch-group/` exists, `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:71-72` must switch to relative imports (`'../swatch-group/swatch'`, `'../swatch-group'`). Per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:110-128`, the `ccExtensibility` resolver runs only in the real app build — Storybook aliases straight to `node_modules` and Vitest doesn't touch it — so leaving the base path would silently render/test the **unstyled base swatch** while the shipped app looks correct.

**Doc drift found:** `overrideStyling.md:129-132` cites `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import as the "known instance, not yet fixed." **There is no `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` on develop at all** — verified. Commit `227171e`'s message independently flags the same thing about `CardBaseline` and `link/index.tsx`.

- **One canonical styling surface per component type** — the theme config, consumed via Chakra's component; never also a `.zimm-*` global class. It deleted ~94 lines of conflicting `.zimm-btn-*` classes to prove the point.

### PR #59 — `feat(footer): SFCC-55 global footer UI`
Merged 2026-08-24, merge commit `8362b3c`, 132 files (+8724/−1187). 13 component `index.tsx`, 9 co-located `.css.ts`, 10 stories, 13 tests.

What it establishes that SFCC-91 must follow:
- **The co-located `<name>.css.ts` pattern.** Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path — co-location is organisational, with no runtime difference. Registration in `theme/components/index.ts` is required either way.
- **Governance follows the file, not the folder** — `CODEOWNERS:186`'s `**/*.css.ts` glob is placed last (last-match-wins) so a co-located recipe drops the Tier 1/2 designer gate.
- **Large recipes decompose** — `theme/components/footer.ts` was split across `footer/footer.css.ts`, `footerNavColumn/`, `bottomBar/` and never landed on develop. `theme/components/button.ts` was deleted and became `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`.
- **Cross-file shared values stay in `theme/components/`** — `footerShared.ts` holds the breakpoints both split files need.
- **Responsive steps are explicit media queries**, not Chakra's array shorthand (the shorthand reintroduces bare token keys at every step and the guard walks responsive arrays).
- **`Zimm*` namespacing is mechanically enforced.** `recipeGuards.test.ts:347`: *"`extendTheme` DEEP MERGES… Anything else must be namespaced (e.g. ZimmFooter, not Footer)."* `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']`.

Registering a key literally named `SwatchGroup` would **silently deep-merge the base recipe** and fail `recipeGuards.test.ts:347`. Name it **`ZimmSwatchGroup`**.
>
> For reference, the base recipe declares `parts: ['swatch','swatchButton']` (`:114`) while its `baseStyle` carries five keys (`swatchGroup`, `swatchLabel`, `swatch`, `swatchesWrapper`, `swatchButton`) — the exact undeclared-parts defect `recipeParts.test.ts` was written to catch.

**PR #64 (SFCC-89)** created the entire `zimmProduct*` family — 7 components × 4 files each, plus `theme/components/index.ts`, `recipeParts.test.ts`, `product-view/index.tsx`, and the PDP page. **PR #68 (SFCC-194)** shows the follow-up shape. Note both also regenerate `.claude/registry/*.md` (auto-generated by `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` on `postinstall`).

### The extension precedent that matters most
Commit `227171e` added `renderHeader?: (props) => React.ReactNode` to `product-view` — a **render slot on the default export**, with a default that reproduces base behaviour exactly. Its message argues the case directly:

> *"overrideStyling.md prescribes putting Zimmermann-only additions behind a named export that wraps the default. ## 7. State of the styling rule — `var(--zimm-*)`

**The rule did reverse, and it reversed inside PR #59 — not in #56.** Verified by `git show e1732a3:.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (PR #56's head), which read:

> ```
> 2. **Semantic colour/spacing token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
>    `spacing="m"`, `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`. These resolve through
>    `theme.colors`/`theme.space` (both registered — see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment
>    for which foundation scales are and aren't registered, and why).
> ```

The reversal commits are `9d5f89c refactor(theme): require var(--zimm-*) over bare Chakra token keys in overrides` and `49a95b9 docs(rules): stop instructing the bare token key the guard now blocks`.

### Current direction on `develop` — `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:14-27`, verbatim

> ```
> 1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
>    All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
> 2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
>    `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
>    token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
>    ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
>    which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
>    is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
>    unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
>    `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
>    enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
>    override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
>    registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
>    that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
> ```

And `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:138-145`:

> ```
> When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
> `iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
> — `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
> `marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
> form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
> used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
> `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
> so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.
> ```

### Recipe or JSX? The rule text and the code disagree — read this carefully

The **rule text is agnostic on location**: hierarchy point 2's examples are written as **JSX props** (`color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`), so on a literal reading `var(--zimm-*)` is permitted in JSX. Point 2 forbids the *bare key*, not the *JSX location*.

But the surrounding rules push everything into the recipe. `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, "One canonical styling surface per component type", verbatim:

> ```
> Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
> either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
> beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
> `<Link>` variant, etc.).
> ```

**The de-facto convention in code is overwhelmingly "recipe", and it is near-absolute.** Verified by grep across `overrides/app/components`:
- **17 `.css.ts` recipe files** contain `var(--zimm-*)`
- **exactly 1 component `.tsx`** contains it (excluding stories/tests): `overrides/app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44` and `:62` — and both are inside a `__css={{ ...styles.part, ...conditional }}` spread, i.e. a conditional the recipe genuinely cannot express, not ordinary styling.

Every `zimmProduct*` component applies styling **only** via `__css={styles.part}` with zero inline token values. So: **put `var(--zimm-*)` in the co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipe.** Reach for a JSX `__css` spread only for a genuinely conditional value, following `footerNavColumn`'s shape.

One caveat the rule states explicitly: the guard *"walks the registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop… apply the same discipline there by hand."* The JSX half is unenforced. Note also `textStyle` stays a bare key — `.claude/rules/css.md` says there is no `var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite expansion.

# SFCC-91 — PreBuild gate (rev 2)

**Story:** PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection
**Depth:** `standard` · **Run date:** 2026-08-31
**Repo state:** `develop` @ `269d5d4`, clean, level with origin
**Scope note:** run as a fresh build. Jhoan's branch and PR #70 deliberately ignored per instruction.

**Rev 2 changes:** Marcel supplied the ACs and 16 Figma node URLs — blockers #1, #2 and #3 are
**resolved**. One **new blocker** surfaced from the PRDs. Two earlier findings were **wrong** and
are corrected below.

---

## Verdict — 🔴 BLOCKED (1 blocker, and it is a doc-integrity stop)

---

## Resolved since rev 1

| # | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🔴 No acceptance criteria | **Resolved.** Five ACs supplied, covering swatch availability, single-colour text-label fallback, selected indication, selection behaviour, and unpopulated index images. |
| 2 | 🔴 Figma unresolvable | **Resolved — and my diagnosis was wrong.** I reported the files as returning stub pages under a View-seat restriction. That was incorrect: `get_metadata` without a node ID only lists top-level pages, and this file's page list is degenerate. Given node IDs, every node resolves. Access was never the problem. |
| 3 | 🔴 Design missing above 4 colours | **Resolved.** `node-id=40001992-51881` — *Colour Options*, `Type=Large (Squared)` and `Type=Small (Rounded)`. |
| 13 | Dependency on SFCC-89 | Confirmed cleared — PR #64 merged 2026-08-27. |

---

## 🔴 The remaining blocker

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 19 | `.docs/prd/` | **Both PRDs say do not build this yet.** `.docs/prd/plp.md` §5.4 (SPR-26 — Open): *"colour swatch creation and management in Business Manager — map colour attribute values… to hex code or swatch image… Colour mapping exercise TBC. **Do not implement until confirmed.**"* Repeated in `.docs/prd/pdp.md:219` Open Items: *"Colour swatch management and mapping — colour mapping exercise TBC (SPR-26, PRD-004)."* And `.docs/prd/pdp.md:17` (PRD-002, confirmed): *"Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names."* The Jira ACs instruct the opposite. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Per AGENTS.md *Doc integrity*: cite the doc, stop, and ask whether the PRD is now stale (SPR-26 resolved by the BM index-image decision) or whether the ticket is running ahead of it. Not a call to make silently. |

---

## 🟡 Clarify

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | AC vs codebase | **The AC's swatch source and the base implementation disagree.** AC: *"the index image for each colour variation is displayed as a swatch."* Base `getVariantValueSwatch` (`hooks/use-variation-attributes.js:26-35`) filters `imageGroups` on **`viewType: 'swatch'`**, not the index image. Either BM populates a `swatch` viewType (base works unchanged) or the index image is a different viewType (custom mapping required). This is the difference between a styling story and a data story. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Confirm which `viewType` BM will actually populate. Directly related to blocker #19. |
| 5 | Confluence / Jira | **PRD-004 is split and only half is deliverable.** PRD-004: *"selecting a colour should update the page content **and URL**"*. The URL/style-code half moved to **SFCC-708** on 2026-08-12 — still **Ready for Development, not started**. Note the new AC says *"the URL updates… **without** full page reload"*, whereas the AC moved to SFCC-708 said *with* a full reload — consistent once split by case, but only if that split is stated. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Confirm: same master ⇒ in-place variant switch (this story); different master/style code ⇒ navigation (SFCC-708). |
| 4 | Confluence | **PRD-004's "Also available in" / "Only available in" copy appears in neither the ticket nor the ACs.** The new AC covers the single-colour case as a text label (*"Colour: Bay Blue"*), which is a different treatment from *"Only available in"*. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Confirm the AC's text-label treatment supersedes PRD-004's wording. |
| 7 | Codebase | **Blast radius exceeds "PDP UI" — but there is now a way to avoid it.** Base `product-tile` also imports `swatch-group` (`index.jsx:29-30`), feeding **PLP** and **every recommendations carousel**. See "Recommended architecture" below: a render slot on `product-view` confines the change to the PDP and avoids overriding `swatch-group` at all. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Pick the architecture. This is the single highest-leverage decision in the story. |
| 8 | CODEOWNERS | **Cross-squad, and squad ownership of the PDP is itself contested.** `swatch-group/` → Squad B + tier-2 + tier-1 (`CODEOWNERS:103`, Tier 2). `pages/product-detail/` → Squad B (`CODEOWNERS:162`) — but `.claude/rules/squadA.md:4,34` claims it for Squad A. The ticket is labelled `Squad-A`. | 🟡 CLARIFY | CODEOWNERS is authoritative for review routing; the squadA.md conflict is a separate governance item. |
| 9 | Confluence | **Design tracker vs ticket.** 04.72 records PDP components finalised **Aug 13** under an explicit *"once locked, no further design changes are permitted"* rule, yet design was pending on Aug 26. The tracker's PDP scope also never lists a colour swatch. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Raise as process drift; does not block this build now that nodes exist. |

---

## 🔵 Notes

| # | Source | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | Figma | **The design's variants do not match the base component's.** `pdp/product-colour-picker` (`40000307:13823`) ships **two sizes × three states**: `Large/Rectangle` (48×72) and `Small/Rounded` (20×24), each in `Unselected` / `Selected` / `Focus`. Base `Swatch` offers `square` \| `circle`. A 48×72 portrait rectangle is not a square and a 20×24 rounded rect is not a circle — so the recipe needs its own variant vocabulary, not the base's. |
| 22 | Figma | **No Hover and no Disabled state exist in the design** — and both absences are *correct*. `.docs/prd/pdp.md:17` states hover-to-preview is *"a custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live"*; and the AC handles unpopulated variations by **not rendering them**, so no disabled state is needed. The design is internally consistent with the PRD here. |
| 23 | Figma | **Placement is fixed.** `Colour Options` sits inside `Content Card and Colour Swatch` at y=126 (218×104), between the product description and the size selector — `40000307:14062`. The PDP content column also carries `Default` / `Warning` / `Unavailable` / `Coming soon` states at desktop **and** mobile. |
| 18 | Codebase | **CORRECTION to rev 1.** I framed the recipe name as a judgement call. It is not — it is mechanically enforced. `recipeGuards.test.ts:351` sets `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` and its comment reads *"Anything else must be namespaced (e.g. ZimmFooter, not Footer)."* Base SFCC registers a `SwatchGroup` recipe, so a key literally named `SwatchGroup` would deep-merge the base and **fail `npm run test`**. Name it **`ZimmSwatchGroup`**. |
| 10 | Codebase | **CORRECTION to rev 1.** I reported that base `Swatch` selects on hover at `lg`+ and implied it affects the PDP. It does not. `swatch.jsx:69` applies the hover handlers only when there is no `href` (`{...(href ? {} : selectHandlers)}`), and `use-variation-attributes.js:152-153` sets `href: null` only in *controlled* mode — the quick-view modals. On the PDP path `href` is a real URL, so swatches are `RouteLink`s and hover-select never fires. Live in quick-view modals only. |
| 11 | Codebase | Base `disabled` is **visual only** — fed to `useMultiStyleConfig` at `swatch.jsx:35`, never spread onto the `<Button>`; no `isDisabled`, no `aria-disabled`, no click guard. Not triggered by this story's ACs (unpopulated variants are not rendered), but PRD-014's disabled *size* swatch will hit it. |
| 15 | Codebase | **Dormant landmine — only if `swatch-group` is overridden.** `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:71-72` imports the swatch by base path. The moment an override exists, those must become `'../swatch-group'` / `'../swatch-group/swatch'` or Storybook and Vitest silently exercise the **base** component. The render-slot architecture sidesteps this entirely. |
| 24 | Codebase | Base recipe `theme/components/project/swatch-group.js` declares `parts: ['swatch','swatchButton']` while its `baseStyle` carries five keys — the exact undeclared-parts defect `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts:101` exists to catch. Declare every part you read. |
| 25 | Docs | **Doc drift.** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:129-132` cites `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import as a "known instance, not yet fixed" — but `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` **does not exist on develop**. |
| 16 | Codebase | On `develop`; the `PreToolUse` hook blocks writes there. `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection` already exists on origin (Jhoan's) — a fresh branch needs a different name. |
| 17 | Docs | `.docs/memory/projectState.md` last updated 2026-08-24; `sprintScope.md` still reads *"Sprint 0 — Foundation"*. Don't scope from either. |

---

## Recommended architecture — a render slot, not a `swatch-group` override

The strongest option, and it dissolves findings #7 and #15 rather than managing them.

Commit `227171e` added `renderHeader?: (props) => React.ReactNode` to the `product-view` override —
a **render slot on the default export**, defaulting to the base behaviour exactly. Its message
argues the case directly:

> *"overrideStyling.md prescribes putting Zimmermann-only additions behind a named export that
> wraps the default. That route cannot express this requirement: a wrapper can only set props the
> default already accepts, so letting a caller replace an internal render block still requires the
> slot on the default. The only alternative is forking the component body, which is a graver
> breach of the faithful-port rule."*

A `renderVariationAttributes` slot is the direct analogue. It means:

- **No `swatch-group` override** → PLP and the recommendations carousels are untouched.
- **No Tier 2 / Squad B file** in the diff, and no cross-squad approval gate.
- **No import-path landmine** (#15) to create and then have to remember.
- A new `ZimmColourSwatch` / `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` in `ui-kits/`, following the
  `zimmProduct*` four-file pattern established by PR #64.

The alternative — a faithful `swatch-group` port plus a `ZimmSwatchGroup` recipe — is the
conventional route, but it changes PLP and every carousel, and needs Squad B plus Tier 2 sign-off.

---

## The build pattern (from PR #64 / SFCC-89, the nearest in-kind precedent)

Four files per component, mirroring `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/`:
`index.tsx` · `index.stories.tsx` · `index.test.tsx` · `<name>.css.ts`, plus one line in
`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

- Recipe key hoisted to a module const; `useMultiStyleConfig(KEY, {...})`.
- Styling applied via `<chakra.x __css={styles.part}>` — never `sx` or style props.
- **`var(--zimm-*)` belongs in the `.css.ts` recipe, not in JSX.** Verified: 17 recipe files use it;
  exactly one component `.tsx` does (`footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`), and only inside a
  `__css={{...styles.part, ...conditional}}` spread the recipe cannot express.
- `textStyle` set in the recipe, and it stays a bare key — there is no `var()` substitute for the
  composite expansion.
- Hooks above any early return; `const intl = useIntl()` then `intl.formatMessage(...)` (never
  destructured — `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`).
- Labels via `react-intl`, **not** `useUiCopy` — `useContentful.ts` sends no `locale`, so `uiCopy`
  would serve the space default to all 8 storefronts.
- Two hard gates on `npm run test`: `recipeParts.test.ts:101` (declared parts must cover every
  `styles.*` read) and `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6 guards, incl. bare-token and namespacing).
- Story title `Commerce/Zimm<Name>`; a `play` where there is interactive behaviour.

**No hook override.** All variation logic funnels through `useDerivedProduct` →

Your ACs and nodes cleared all three blockers. But the last agent found a **new one**, and I owe you two corrections.

## Corrections first

**My Figma diagnosis was wrong.** I said the files returned stub pages because your seat is View-only. That wasn't it — `get_metadata` without a node ID just lists top-level pages, and this file's page list is degenerate. Given your node IDs, every node resolves cleanly. Access was never the problem.

**Hover-select doesn't affect the PDP.** I flagged base `Swatch` selecting on hover at `lg`+. It only binds those handlers when there's no `href` — and on the PDP path `href` is a real URL, so swatches are `RouteLink`s. Hover-select is live in the quick-view modals only. `.docs/prd/pdp.md:17` confirms hover-preview is out of scope for go-live, so the design correctly has no hover state.

**And one thing I under-called:** I framed the recipe name as a judgement call. It isn't. `recipeGuards.test.ts:351` sets `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — anything else must be namespaced. Base SFCC registers a `SwatchGroup` recipe, so that key would deep-merge the base and **fail `npm run test`**. It has to be `ZimmSwatchGroup`.

## 🔴 The new blocker — both PRDs say don't build this yet

`.docs/prd/plp.md` §5.4 (SPR-26 — Open), verbatim:

> *"colour swatch creation and management in Business Manager — map colour attribute values (e.g. Floral, Cream) to hex code or swatch image… Colour mapping exercise TBC. **Do not implement until confirmed.**"*

Repeated at `.docs/prd/pdp.md:219`. And PRD-002 (confirmed) states *"Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names."*

Your ACs instruct the opposite. AGENTS.md's Doc integrity rule says to stop and cite rather than pick a side.

**There's a concrete technical edge to this too.** Your AC says the **index image** is the swatch. Base `getVariantValueSwatch` filters `imageGroups` on **`viewType: 'swatch'`** — a different thing. If BM populates a `swatch` viewType this is a styling story; if the index image is a different viewType, it's a data-mapping story. That's the SPR-26 mapping exercise, unresolved.

## The good news — the design is clear and there's a better architecture

`pdp/product-colour-picker` gives **two sizes × three states**: `Large/Rectangle` (48×72) and `Small/Rounded` (20×24), each Unselected / Selected / Focus. No hover, no disabled — both correctly absent. It sits between the description and size selector, 218×104.

The base's `square`/`circle` don't match a 48×72 portrait rectangle, so the recipe needs its own vocabulary regardless.

**And the strongest option avoids the PLP problem entirely.** Rather than overriding `swatch-group` (which base `product-tile` also uses → PLP + every carousel, Tier 2, Squad B sign-off), use a `renderVariationAttributes` **render slot** on `product-view` — the exact pattern commit `227171e` established with `renderHeader`. No shared file touched, no cross-squad gate, no import landmine.

name: scope-check
description: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
---

Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs.

The prompt to check is: $ARGUMENTS

## What to do

1. **Identify every file the prompt would likely touch** — both files named explicitly and files Claude would naturally reach through refactoring upward, shared imports, or "while I'm in here" changes.

2. **Classify each file by tier**:
   - Tier 1 (Frozen) — see [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md)
   - Tier 2 (Protected) — see [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md)
   - Tier 3 (Squad-owned) — see `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `.claude/rules/squadB.md` *(if absent, infer from path: checkout/cart/payments = Squad A; PDP/PLP/search/account = Squad B)*
   - Tier 4 (Feature-local, safe)

3. **Assess the risk**:
   - Is the prompt open-ended in a way that lets Claude drift into shared code?
   - Could Claude refactor upward into hooks or utilities not mentioned?
   - Does it cross squad boundaries (Squad A territory + Squad B territory in the same prompt)?
   - Does it name specific files, or just a feature area?

4. **Verdict**: output one of:
   - ✅ SAFE — clearly scoped, no Tier 1 or 2 risk
   - ⚠️ RISKY — likely to drift, needs a rewrite before running
   - 🚫 BLOCKED — requires Tier 1 modification, stop and get owner approval first

5. **If RISKY or BLOCKED**, rewrite the prompt so it is safely scoped:
   - Name exact file paths under `overrides/app/...`
   - End with "Do not modify any other files"
   - Split cross-squad work into two separate prompts

## Output format

Use a compact table for the file/tier list. One short paragraph for the verdict. If rewriting, show the improved prompt in a code block.

### Files at risk of drift (named so they can be excluded)

| `overrides/app/components/swatch-group/` | **2** — Squad B | The "obvious" override. Base `product-tile:29-30` also imports it → changes **PLP and every recommendations carousel** |

| `overrides/app/hooks/*`, base variation hooks | — | Hard Rule #5 (never refactor upward). Base hooks reach through the `hooks/index.js` barrel and would not resolve in Storybook/Vitest anyway |

      commit body that this file was touched and why.
  overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx
    → add ONE optional prop, `renderVariationAttributes`, mirroring the existing
      `renderHeader` slot in this same file (type on ProductViewProps, default that
      renders the current inline block unchanged, call site swapped to the slot).

      formatting, no comment edits, no type tightening, no unrelated fixes.
  overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx
    → pass the slot. Nothing else.

  - Sizes: Large/Rectangle 48x72, Small/Rounded 20x24. States: Unselected, Selected, Focus.

content.text:
Right — and reading it properly has changed my view of my own recommendation. Here's the thing I'd missed.

## The block renders colour *and* size through the same component

`product-view/index.tsx:785` loops over **all** `variationAttributes`, not just colour:

```
variationAttributes.map(({ id, name, selectedValue, values }) => { ... })
```

Colour and size both come out of that one loop, both wrapped in `<SwatchGroup>`, with the only difference being line 820:

```
variant={id === 'color' ? 'circle' : 'square'}
```

Colour gets `circle`, size gets `square`. That single fact reshapes both routes.

## What it does to the `swatch-group` override

It's worse than I said. Overriding `swatch-group` doesn't just reach PDP + PLP + carousels — **it also changes the size selector**, because size renders through the same component. So a change scoped in the ticket as "colour swatches" would touch four surfaces, one of which (size) has its own separate design in Figma with its own states — `pdp/size-selector` has default/filled/active/error, and `pdp/size-selector/item` has in-stock / low-stock / out-of-stock / recommended / notify-me. That is not a swatch. It's a different component that hasn't been built yet.

So the size selector is going to move *off* swatch-group eventually. Coupling colour to swatch-group now means doing that work twice.

## What it does to my slot recommendation

My proposed `renderVariationAttributes` slot would replace **the whole loop** — which puts the size selector in SFCC-91's scope. That's wrong; it's out of scope and undesigned as a swatch.

The slot needs to be **per-attribute**, not per-block. Called once inside the loop with what the loop already destructures, defaulting to the current markup:

```
renderVariationAttribute?: (attr: SfccVariationAttribute) => React.ReactNode
```

Then SFCC-91's implementation handles `id === 'color'` and returns `undefined` for everything else, so size falls through to the untouched base rendering. Colour becomes Zimmermann; size stays exactly as it is until its own story.

## The honest argument against the slot

I should give you this rather than just advocate. `overrideStyling.md`'s bridge pattern says Zimmermann-only additions belong behind a **named export that wraps the default**, not on the default itself. Commit `227171e` already argued its way past that for `renderHeader` — a wrapper can only set props the default accepts, so replacing an internal render block genuinely requires a slot.

That reasoning holds for a second slot too. But **two additive props on a "faithful port" starts to look like a fork by increments**, and there's no third one that's obviously fine. At some point the honest move is either a real Zimmermann PDP component or a documented decision that `product-view` is now a slot-based host. Right now nobody has made that call — I'd be making it implicitly by adding the second slot.

That's the actual trade, and it's a judgement about direction rather than a technical constraint.

## Two smaller things that bear on it

**The AC's "not populated" and the base's `disabled` are different conditions.** Line 817 passes `disabled={!orderable}` — stock availability. Your AC is about an *index image not being populated* — a content condition. Neither route gets that for free; it's new logic either way.

**`backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}`** at line 797 is doing something slightly alarming — using the colour's display name as a raw CSS colour keyword behind the image. For "Bay Blue" that resolves to nothing; for "Ivory" it resolves to a real CSS colour. It's inherited base behaviour, marked `audit-allow` as verbatim, so it's not yours — but whichever route you take, that line is in the blast radius and worth a decision rather than a copy.

What's your instinct on the direction question — is `product-view` allowed to become a slot host, or would you rather that conversation happen explicitly before a second slot lands?

'circle' : 'square'}`.   renderVariationAttribute?: (attr: SfccVariationAttribute) => React.ReactNode
called once inside the existing loop, defaulting to the current inline markup so behaviour is unchanged when omitted. The PDP passes an implementation that handles `id === 'color'` and returns undefined/falls through for everything else, so size renders exactly as it does today.

  overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts}

**There is no unit-test coverage percentage for the PWA frontend repo (this repo).** Testing is deliberately risk-based, not percentage-based. Re-verified 2026-08-06 by an exhaustive triangulated scan (codebase+config, Confluence 14 CQL / full 185-page tree, Jira 22 JQL / all 4 projects) — all three surfaces agree.

- This PWA repo: `test` = `vitest run` (no `--coverage`), no `test:coverage` script, no `@vitest/coverage-*` installed, `vitest.config.ts` has no `coverage` thresholds (+ `passWithNoTests: true`), no codecov/sonar/.nycrc, and `qa.yml`'s `unit-tests` job just runs `npm test` (pass/fail, no coverage gate). SIT gate + deploy workflows reference unit tests not at all. `.claude/rules/testing.md` + AGENTS.md: "Write tests only where failure would be non-obvious or costly to debug."
- **Actual inventory as of 2026-08-06:** only **2** unit-test files exist repo-wide, both hooks — `useCountryConfig.test.ts` (10 tests) + `useContentfulClient.test.ts` (5 tests) = **15 tests**. Plus 2 stories (0 `play()` fns) and 1 Playwright smoke spec. ~51 source files under `overrides/app`; file-presence proxy ≈ 3.9%. Untested logic-and-risk hotspots: the Tier 1 `overrides/app/ssr/` helpers (CSP, SLAS auth, payment metadata) and the pages/.
- The **90% coverage threshold** people sometimes cite lives on Confluence page "SFCC Build and Deployment Process – Headless Architecture" (264896514) — but that page **explicitly scopes itself to the SFCC *backend* cartridge repo** (`zimmermann-sfcc/`, Jest with `dw.*` mocks, `ci.yml`/`pr-check.yml`, `cartridges/`/`vendor/`). It says the frontend is documented separately. That 90% does **not** apply to the PWA. (Diagnostic proof: Confluence queries for `Jest`, `test:coverage`, and the exact phrase "branches functions lines statements" each return ONLY page 264896514.)
- PWA-specific Confluence pages (PWA CI/CD Pipeline 305561601, Development Standards 261750785, Human-in-the-Lead 305102849) require unit tests to *pass*; none state a coverage %.
- Jira: no issue defines a coverage target for either repo. **Two false positives to ignore next time:** (a) `Lighthouse CI >90` in epic SFCC-1 is a *performance* score, not coverage; (b) the sole "coverage" mention (SFCC-205) means *Figma-to-code design-handover* coverage. No dedicated Testing/QA epic exists; unit tests appear only as an unquantified pipeline step in SFCC-1.

**Why:** Both repos live in the same SFCC Confluence space, so the backend's 90% Jest threshold is easy to misread as a frontend requirement.
**How to apply:** If asked for the PWA's coverage target, answer "none — risk-based selective testing." Don't wire a coverage threshold into `vitest.config.ts`/`qa.yml` on the strength of the 90% Confluence figure. Related: [[reference-confluence-sfcc]].

# SFCC-91 — Build plan

**Story:** PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection
**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches` (deliberately not the other developer's branch name)
**Baseline:** `develop` @ `269d5d4` — `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run test` 26 files / 408 tests green
**Architecture:** per-attribute render slot on `product-view`. Decided by Marcel 2026-08-31. Not revisited.

---

## 1. Goal

Build SFCC-91 to the five Jira ACs and the Figma `pdp/product-colour-picker` design, using a new
namespaced theme recipe plus a new atom and molecule under `ui-kits/`, consumed through a new
per-attribute render slot on the already-overridden `product-view` — with zero change to
`swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `translations/`, `theme/foundation/`, or any hook.

## 2. Scale — one branch, four commits

The three modified files cannot be usefully separated. The theme registration is 4 lines and would
otherwise register recipes that don't exist; the slot has no value without its consumer, and the
consumer has no mount point without the slot. Two code-owner teams on one PR is normal and is what
CODEOWNERS is for.

Hard Rule 10 (more than one protection tier) is satisfied by the manifest being fixed and
enumerated up front. The Tier 2 file must still be named in the commit body and the PR body.

| Step | Loop depth | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — slot | Light: implement → `tsc`/`lint`/`test` → diff review | Mechanical, behaviour-preserving by construction. Its one failure mode (a non-verbatim edit) is caught by reading the diff, not a test. |
| 2 — atom | Full loop, one revision cycle | Real branching, a new recipe, three guard suites. |
| 3 — molecule | Full loop, one revision cycle | Carries AC 1, 3 and 5 as branch logic plus roving focus. Highest defect density. |
| 4 — wiring | Light + developer visual check | ~15 lines of prop mapping; the behaviour is proven by 2 and 3. |

**Dropped deliberately:** no `.feature`/Playwright spec. `testing.md`'s gherkin workflow needs Lead
QA sign-off first, and `pdp` has no allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes`, so a new spec
would resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and never run pre-merge. **AC 4 (no full page reload) is
genuinely an E2E assertion — this is a real coverage gap, not a free skip.** Raise as a follow-up.

## 3. File manifest

  rendering nothing: the shopper still needs to know what they're viewing, and the colour *name* is
  product data, not image data.

content.text:
## PreBuild complete — SFCC-91

**The gate is clear. No 🔴 remain.** Plan and findings are at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-91/`. Repo untouched throughout — `git status` clean.

### One thing worth leading with

The last check I ran overturned a decision the plan had already made. The planner, reasoning from the container being 192×104, concluded the ">4 colours" design couldn't wrap and defaulted to `flexWrap: 'wrap'`.

I read the node instead of reasoning about it. Both variants contain a **`Pagination` frame with left/right chevrons** above a fixed **four-swatch window**. The >4 treatment is **pagination**, not wrapping. That default would have shipped the wrong behaviour and it would have looked correct in review.

The icon dependency is already satisfied — `ChevronLeftIcon` / `ChevronRightIcon` exist in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`, Zimmermann-drawn from Figma. Step 3 now carries the pagination controls, their a11y, and a `ZimmIcon` mock in its Vitest test.

### The plan

**One branch, four commits.** `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches`.

| | Count | Tier exposure |
|---|---|---|
| New files | 8 | All Tier 3, squad-a + squad-b |
| Modified | 3 | **1 × Tier 2** (`theme/components/index.ts`), 1 × Tier 3 (`product-detail`, squad-b), 1 × unowned (`product-view` — in neither tier file nor CODEOWNERS) |

Steps 2 and 3 run the full implementer→tester→scorer loop with one revision cycle budgeted; steps 1 and 4 are single-pass with a diff review. A third cycle on 2 or 3 means a missing Figma value or a wrong architectural read — stop, don't iterate.

**Two constraints the planner found that I'd missed:**
- `recipeParts.test.ts` fails on a recipe with no sibling `index.tsx`, so recipe + component + registration must land in **one commit**, not three.
- **There is no border-radius token anywhere in `theme/foundation/`.** The `Small/Rounded` variant can't be built without a Tier 1 addition, and it has no PDP consumer — so it's excluded, with the reason recorded in the recipe. That's a scope reduction against a designed variant; your call whether to accept it.
- Also neat: 72px has no token either (gap between 64 and 140), so height comes from `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` on the 48px token rather than a raw literal. Passes `audit:tokens` cleanly.

### Still open — carried as stated assumptions, not resolved

1. **Does BM return "Colour" or "Color"** as the attribute display name on AU? AC 1's example is "Colour: Bay Blue" and the label comes from BM data. Hardcoding "Colour" would break the other ten locales, so this needs the attribute owner, not a code fix.
2. **Does the "Colour: `<name>`" label persist in the multi-colour case?** AC 1 specifies it only for single-colour. Default is to keep it; confirmed during the Step 3 Figma read.
3. **`viewType: 'swatch'` vs the index image** — still the one that decides whether this is a styling story or a data story.
4. **AC 4 has no automated coverage.** No-full-reload is genuinely an E2E assertion, and a new `pdp` spec would hit `e2e_scope: skip` because `qa.yml` has no `pdp` allow-list group. Step 4 is explicitly **PASS-pending-your-visual-confirmation**, not PASS — the tester is instructed not to claim it from a terminal.

### Ready for Build

Baseline is green (408 tests, `tsc` clean), so anything red afterwards is Build's doing. Two things before you invoke it: you're on `develop`, so a branch is needed first, and `zimmerMANNPreBuild` stops here by design — Build is your call, not mine.

## What the API said

**1. BM returns "Colour", not "Color".** Product `8637DS241` on the dev tier returns:

variationAttributes[0]  id='color'   name='Colour'   values=1  → 'BLUBIR' / 'Blue Birds'

```

So AC 1's literal *"Colour: Bay Blue"* falls straight out of `attr.name`. No hardcoding, no locale risk, no BM change. The SFCC key stays US-spelled `color` — exactly the split the plan already assumed.

**2. `viewType: 'swatch'` exists and is populated — and this is a styling story, not a data story.** But the mechanism has a catch worth knowing:

| Request | imageGroups | `swatch` groups |
|---|---|---|
| without `allImages` | 4 | 1 — **no `variationAttributes`** |
| `allImages=true` | 8 | 2 — one carrying `variationAttributes: color=['BLUBIR']` |

Base `getVariantValueSwatch` filters on `viewType:'swatch'` **and** `variationValues:{color: value}`. That second condition only matches the group that appears **when `allImages=true`**. Without the flag, every colour's `image` comes back `undefined` — and under the plan's AC 5 filter, *no swatches would render at all*.

The PDP already passes it: `product-detail/index.tsx:220`, on the main `useProduct`. (The `allImages: false` at `:282` is the set/bundle child fetch, already out of scope.) So no fetch change is needed, and SFCC-91 adds no new exposure to the `allImages` behaviour recorded under SFCC-29 — it's already how the PDP loads.

Standing risk now noted in the plan: flip `:220` to `false` and every swatch silently vanishes. That deserves an inline comment at the call site.

**3. The label persists in the multi-colour case** — answered from Figma, not API. `40000307:13867`'s `labelContainer` holds a `Label group` with **two text nodes** (36px + 96px — "Colour:" and the value) next to `Pagination`, sitting directly above the four-swatch row. So it's present in the multi-colour design too.

And `Small/Rounded` is recorded as out of scope per your call, with the no-radius-token reason kept in the recipe so it isn't rediscovered later.

## One honest limitation

The dev catalogue has exactly **one** searchable product, with **one** colour. So I've verified the *mechanism* end to end, but multi-colour rendering, pagination past four, and AC 5's unpopulated case have not been exercised against real data — only fixtures will cover them until Step 4 runs against a richer tier. Not quite — there's **one genuine decision left** that I raised earlier and you haven't ruled on. Everything else is either answered or is a known risk rather than a choice.

First, the token check came back clean: all seven the plan names exist, and I confirmed the 72px gap is real across the *named* scale too (`4xl`=64px → `5xl`=80px, and the numeric aliases jump 52→140). So the `aspectRatio: '2/3'` workaround is necessary rather than clever, and Build won't stall on it. No radius token anywhere, which independently validates dropping `Small/Rounded`.

## The open decision — cross-product colours

PRD-004 says the PDP should show **"Also available in" / "Only available in"** colour swatches. Neither phrase appears in your ACs, and they describe a different thing from same-master variants: linking *separate master products* that aren't natural colour variants of each other. That's exactly what **SFCC-708** exists for — the Related Colours BM attribute — and it's **Ready for Development, not started** (Victor).

So: does SFCC-91 render **only this master's own colour variations**, or does it also need the cross-product "Also available in" treatment?

My read is same-master only — AC 2 says *"the index image for each colour variation"*, which is this product's variations, and cross-product linking has its own ticket and a BM attribute that doesn't exist yet. The plan is written that way. But that's currently an assumption I made, not a call you made, and it changes what "done" means for PRD-004.

## Four things that aren't decisions, but you should know before Build

1. **Build does two Figma reads that can still stop it.** Steps 2 and 3 open the swatch states and the container to record border width, colour, focus offset, `itemSpacing` and padding. The *token vocabulary* exists, but the actual Figma values are unread — if one doesn't map, the step is instructed to stop and ask rather than invent. That's the intended behaviour, but it means Build may pause rather than run clean.
2. **AC 4 has no automated coverage**, deliberately. A new `pdp` spec would resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` because `qa.yml` has no `pdp` allow-list group. Step 4 is PASS-*pending your visual confirmation*, not PASS.
3. **Step 4 needs your dev server.** I won't run `npm start` — five-point checklist is in the plan.
4. **PR #70 already exists for SFCC-91.** Fine for this test run since we're ignoring it, but in reality a second PR on the same ticket is a collision worth resolving with Jhoan first.
